t: 要約：道案内アプリと認知地図
p: When people navigate with turn-by-turn directions on a phone, they reliably reach their destinations, yet they often cannot retrace the route afterwards. Researchers who study spatial cognition explain this not as a failure of memory but as a consequence of what attention is asked to do. A traveller following instructions attends to the next command rather than to the relations among landmarks, and it is precisely those relations, not the landmarks themselves, from which a mental map is built. In this sense the device does not weaken a faculty so much as relieve it of the very work through which it develops. Some critics conclude that we should abandon such tools altogether, but this is to mistake the problem. The aim is not to refuse assistance but to decide which kinds of effort are worth preserving. A driver delivering parcels in an unfamiliar city may gain nothing from building a mental map she will never use again, whereas a child learning to move around her own neighbourhood may lose a great deal. The question, then, is not whether technology makes us less capable, but which capacities we are willing to let it carry for us, and under what circumstances.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 道案内に従うと注意が目印どうしの関係から離れるため頭の中の地図が育たないが、問題は道具を拒むことではなく、どの場面でどの能力の働きを道具に任せるかを見極めることである。
道案内アプリは人間の記憶力そのものを衰えさせるので、とくに子どもには使わせないようにすべきである。
頭の中の地図は目印を一つ一つ覚えることで作られるので、アプリを使う人も目印を意識して記憶する努力をすべきである。
配達員と子どもではアプリの使い方が異なり、技術が年齢によって異なる影響を与えることが分かる。
e: 本文は、①道案内に従うと注意が「次の指示」に向き、地図の材料である目印どうしの関係に向かない、②だから能力は「弱まる」というより育つための作業を免除される、③道具を捨てよという結論は問題の取り違えで、どの努力を残すかを場面ごとに決めることが大切、という流れです。正解はこの三点を押さえています。「記憶力そのものを衰えさせる」は本文が否定する見方（not as a failure of memory）、「目印を覚える」は not the landmarks themselves に反します。配達員と子どもは「場面による違い」の例であり、年齢差が主題ではありません。
m: 要約は「現象→原因→誤った結論の否定→筆者の問い」の順で

q: 本文中の this is to mistake the problem（第5文）について、筆者がそのように述べる理由として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Because the real issue is not whether to use assistance at all, but which forms of mental effort deserve to be kept in which situations.
Because the critics have failed to notice that navigation devices actually improve people's memory of landmarks.
Because abandoning navigation devices would make it impossible for delivery drivers to do their jobs.
Because the critics confuse the memory of routes with the memory of the people one meets on the way.
e: 直後の文 The aim is not to refuse assistance but to decide which kinds of effort are worth preserving が理由そのものです。「道具を捨てるか否か」ではなく「どの努力を残すか」が問題だ、というのが筆者の立場です。道具が目印の記憶を「改善する」とは書かれていません。配達員の例は「地図を作っても得るものがない場面」の例で、仕事ができなくなるという話ではありません。出会う人の記憶の話は本文にありません。
m: not A but B の B に筆者の主張がある

t: 要約：間接的な言い方の二つの機能
p: Why do people so often say less than they mean? A request phrased as a question—'Would you mind closing the window?'—is, strictly speaking, inefficient: it takes longer to say than a direct command and risks being misunderstood. Linguists have long explained such indirectness as a form of politeness, a way of leaving the listener room to refuse without either party losing face. But this explanation, though correct as far as it goes, overlooks a second function. Indirect speech allows a speaker to say something while preserving the possibility of denying that it was said. A suggestion that a permit might be approved more quickly if a gift were offered, a remark to a reluctant witness about how much he must love his children, an invitation to stay for 'one more drink' at the end of an evening: in each case the speaker communicates clearly enough to be understood, yet not so clearly that the meaning could be proved. Indirectness, on this view, is not only a courtesy extended to the listener but also a protection the speaker extends to himself.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 間接的な言い方には、聞き手が断る余地を残す礼儀としての働きに加えて、話し手が後で自分の意図を否認できる余地を残すという自己防衛の働きもある。
間接的な言い方は時間がかかり誤解も招くので、はっきりした命令や依頼に置き換えるべきである。
言語学者の「礼儀」という説明は誤りであり、間接的な言い方の本当の働きは話し手の自己防衛だけである。
間接的な言い方は、賄賂や脅しなど不正な目的をもつ場面に限って用いられる。
e: 本文は「礼儀という従来の説明は、それなりに正しいが（correct as far as it goes）第二の働きを見落としている」と述べ、その第二の働き＝「言ったことを否認できる可能性を残す」ことを、贈り物で許可が早まるというほのめかしなどの例で示し、最後に not only A but also B でまとめています。正解はこの両方を含みます。「置き換えるべき」という主張はありません。従来の説明を「誤り」とし「だけ」と限定する選択肢は、not only … but also の構造に反します。賄賂などは例であり、用いられる場面を限定してはいません。
m: correct as far as it goes＝部分的には正しい

q: この英文の議論の進め方を説明したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: An accepted explanation is granted to be partly right, and then an additional function is proposed and illustrated with examples.
Two rival explanations are presented, and the author concludes that neither of them can be correct.
A common practice is criticised as inefficient, and the author recommends a more direct way of speaking.
The history of a linguistic theory is traced from its origins to its eventual rejection by most scholars.
e: 第3文で従来の「礼儀」説を挙げ、第4文で though correct as far as it goes（それなりに正しいが）と一部を認めたうえで a second function を示し、具体例（贈り物で許可が早まるというほのめかし、証人への遠回しの脅し）で裏づけています。二つの説をどちらも否定してはいません。冒頭の「非効率」は問題提起であり、直接的な話し方を勧めてはいません。学説の歴史を追う文章でもありません。
m: 譲歩（認める）→新しい論点→具体例→まとめ

t: 要約：観光と「本物」の文化
p: Tourists often complain that the places they visit have been spoiled by tourism: that the traditional festival has become a performance staged for cameras, and that the old market now sells souvenirs instead of vegetables. The complaint assumes that there was once an authentic version of the place, untouched by outsiders, which the visitor has arrived just too late to see. Yet most of the traditions that tourists seek were themselves shaped by earlier contact, trade, and migration; the 'unspoiled' village of one century was frequently the bustling crossroads of another. To demand that a culture remain as it was at some arbitrary moment is to deny its members the right to change that every living culture exercises. The more interesting question is not whether a place has changed, but who has had a say in how it changed.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 観光客が惜しむ「本物」の姿は、外部との交流の中で変わり続けてきた文化の一時点を恣意的に固定したものにすぎず、問うべきは変化の有無ではなく変化のあり方を誰が決めたかである。
観光は伝統文化を損なうので、観光客の数を制限して土地の本来の姿を守るべきである。
どの文化も外部との接触から生まれた以上、伝統という考え方そのものに意味はない。
観光客は訪れるのが遅すぎたため、手つかずの本物の文化を見る機会を失ってしまった。
e: 本文は、①観光客の不満は「かつて手つかずの本物があった」という前提に立つ、②しかし伝統の多くは交易や移住などの接触で形づくられてきた、③ある時点の姿にとどまれと求めるのは変化する権利の否定、④問うべきは「誰が変化に関わったか」、という流れです。正解はこれを押さえています。観光客の数の制限は主張していません。「伝統に意味はない」は言い過ぎです。最後の選択肢は筆者が批判する前提そのものです。
m: 筆者が批判する「前提」を見抜くことが要約の鍵

t: 論旨：筆者が批判する前提
p: Tourists often complain that the places they visit have been spoiled by tourism: that the traditional festival has become a performance staged for cameras, and that the old market now sells souvenirs instead of vegetables. The complaint assumes that there was once an authentic version of the place, untouched by outsiders, which the visitor has arrived just too late to see. Yet most of the traditions that tourists seek were themselves shaped by earlier contact, trade, and migration; the 'unspoiled' village of one century was frequently the bustling crossroads of another. q: 筆者が批判している考え方として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: The belief that a culture possesses a fixed, original form which any change necessarily corrupts.
The belief that local people should have a voice in deciding how their town develops.
The belief that trade and migration have influenced traditions in many parts of the world.
The belief that markets selling vegetables are more useful to residents than souvenir shops.
e: 第2文 The complaint assumes that there was once an authentic version of the place, untouched by outsiders が批判の対象である前提です。第3・4文でこれを「伝統自体が接触で形づくられた」「ある時点に固定せよと求めるのは変化の権利の否定」と退けています。「地元の人が変化に関わるべき」は最終文が示す筆者自身の関心に近く、批判の対象ではありません。交易や移住の影響は筆者が根拠として使っている事実です。野菜と土産物の有用性は論じていません。
m: The complaint assumes… の「前提」が批判の標的

t: 要約：プライバシーと文脈
p: 'If you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear.' The argument is persuasive because it frames privacy as the concern of people with something shameful to conceal. Yet privacy has less to do with secrecy than with control over context. Most of us are willing to tell our doctors things we would never tell our employers, and to share with close friends details we would not want published. Nothing in this information is necessarily shameful; what matters is who knows it and for what purpose. The harm of surveillance, then, lies not chiefly in the exposure of secrets but in the collapse of the separate contexts in which we present ourselves differently—and legitimately so—to different people.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: プライバシーの核心は秘密を隠すことより、情報を誰が何のために知るかという文脈を自分で管理することにあり、監視の害は相手ごとに異なる自己の示し方を成り立たせる文脈の区別を壊す点にある。
隠すべきことがない人は監視を恐れる必要がないので、プライバシーを強く主張するのはやましい人だけである。
医師や友人には何を話してもよいが、雇用主には個人的な情報を一切伝えてはならない。
監視の最大の害は、恥ずべき秘密が公になり、本人の評判が損なわれることにある。
e: 第3文 privacy has less to do with secrecy than with control over context（秘密よりも文脈の管理に関わる）が主張の中心で、医師・雇用主・友人の例で説明し、最終文で監視の害を「秘密の暴露」ではなく「文脈の区別の崩壊」だとしています。2番目は筆者が反論している主張そのものです。3番目は例を規範に取り違えています。4番目は not chiefly in the exposure of secrets に反します。
m: less A than B＝AというよりむしろB

t: 論旨：反論される主張の説得力
p: 'If you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear.' The argument is persuasive because it frames privacy as the concern of people with something shameful to conceal. Yet privacy has less to do with secrecy than with control over context. Most of us are willing to tell our doctors things we would never tell our employers, and to share with close friends details we would not want published. Nothing in this information is necessarily shameful; what matters is who knows it and for what purpose. The harm of surveillance, then, lies not chiefly in the exposure of secrets but in the collapse of the separate contexts in which we present ourselves differently—and legitimately so—to different people.
q: 筆者によれば、冒頭の主張（'If you have nothing to hide...'）が説得力をもってしまうのはなぜか。最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Because it presents privacy as something that matters only to people who have shameful secrets.
Because most people really do have nothing that they would prefer to keep private.
Because surveillance has in fact rarely caused harm to ordinary citizens.
Because it correctly identifies the collapse of contexts as the main danger of surveillance.
e: 第2文 The argument is persuasive because it frames privacy as the concern of people with something shameful to conceal が直接の根拠です。プライバシーを「やましい人の問題」という枠にはめるから説得力があるように見える、という指摘です。多くの人に隠したいことがない、監視の害は少ない、とは書かれていません。文脈の崩壊は筆者自身の主張で、冒頭の主張が見抜いている点ではありません。
m: frame A as B＝AをBという枠で捉えさせる

t: 要約：学習の手ごたえと定着
p: Students who reread their notes before an examination usually feel that they are learning, and teachers who explain material with great clarity are usually rated highly. Both impressions are understandable, and both can be misleading. A large body of research suggests that the conditions which make learning feel smooth are often not the conditions under which it lasts. Material that is easy to process at the moment of study tends to be forgotten quickly, while material that requires effort to retrieve—because it was tested, spaced out over time, or mixed with other topics—tends to endure. The difficulty is that the beneficial kind of struggle feels like failure while it is happening. A learner who judges her progress by how fluent she feels will therefore systematically choose the methods that serve her least.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 学習が順調だと感じられる条件と知識が定着する条件は一致しないことが多く、思い出す努力を要する方法ほど定着するが、その苦労は失敗のように感じられるため、手ごたえで進歩を測る学習者は効果の薄い方法を選びがちである。
ノートの読み返しや分かりやすい説明は、学習を定着させる最も確実な方法である。
学習はつねに苦痛を伴うべきであり、楽しく感じられる学習には効果がない。
教師の評価は説明の分かりやすさではなく、生徒の試験の点数だけで決めるべきである。
e: 本文は、①読み返しや明快な説明は「学べている」感覚を生むが誤解を招きうる、②スムーズに感じる条件と定着する条件は別、③テスト・分散・混ぜ合わせなど思い出す努力が必要な学習ほど残る、④その苦労は失敗のように感じられるので、流暢さで進歩を判断すると逆効果の方法を選ぶ、という流れです。2番目は本文が否定する印象です。3番目は「つねに苦痛」と一般化しすぎです。教師の評価方法の提案はありません。
m: 感じる手ごたえ≠実際の定着

t: 論旨：結論文の意味
p: Students who reread their notes before an examination usually feel that they are learning, and teachers who explain material with great clarity are usually rated highly. Both impressions are understandable, and both can be misleading. A large body of research suggests that the conditions which make learning feel smooth are often not the conditions under which it lasts. Material that is easy to process at the moment of study tends to be forgotten quickly, while material that requires effort to retrieve—because it was tested, spaced out over time, or mixed with other topics—tends to endure. The difficulty is that the beneficial kind of struggle feels like failure while it is happening. A learner who judges her progress by how fluent she feels will therefore systematically choose the methods that serve her least.
q: 最終文 A learner who judges her progress by how fluent she feels will therefore systematically choose the methods that serve her least. の内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Since effective methods feel like failure, a learner who trusts her sense of ease will consistently prefer the less effective ones.
A learner who speaks fluently will always make faster progress than one who struggles.
Learners who judge their own progress carefully will usually choose the best methods.
Because fluency is the goal of learning, methods that produce it quickly should be chosen.
e: therefore が前文 the beneficial kind of struggle feels like failure while it is happening を受けています。有益な苦労は「失敗している感じ」を伴うので、「すらすらできる感じ」で進歩を判断すると、いちばん役に立たない方法を一貫して（systematically）選んでしまう、という意味です。fluent は「話すのが流暢」ではなく「処理がすらすら進む感覚」です。3・4番目は本文の結論と逆です。
m: therefore は直前の文を受ける

t: 要約：地図と科学モデル
p: A map that showed everything would be useless. To be of any help, a map must leave out almost all of what it represents—the individual trees, the colour of the doors, the people in the streets—and the choice of what to omit depends on the purpose for which it is made. A subway diagram that distorts distances beyond recognition may be the best possible guide for a passenger, and the worst possible guide for someone walking above ground. Scientific models work in much the same way. They are often criticised for being unrealistic, as though their simplifications were an embarrassing compromise. But a model's value lies precisely in what it ignores, provided that what it ignores does not matter for the question being asked. The proper objection to a model, then, is never simply that it is unrealistic, but that it is unrealistic in the wrong respects.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 地図が目的に応じて大半を省くからこそ役立つように、科学のモデルも問いに関係のないものを無視する点に価値があり、批判すべきは非現実的であることそのものではなく、問いにとって重要な点で現実から外れていることである。
科学のモデルは現実を単純化しすぎているので、できるだけ多くの要素を取り込んで現実に近づけるべきである。
地下鉄の路線図は距離を正しく表していないので、乗客にとっても歩行者にとっても不便である。
地図とモデルはどちらも現実を正確に写すことを目的としており、省略はやむを得ない妥協である。
e: 本文は地図の比喩から入り、「何を省くかは目的で決まる」と述べたうえで科学モデルに当てはめ、「モデルの価値は無視するものにこそある（問いに関係しない限り）」「正当な批判は誤った点で非現実的なことだ」と結論します。2番目は筆者が退ける批判の立場です。路線図は乗客には最良の案内になりうると書かれています。4番目の「やむを得ない妥協」は as though … an embarrassing compromise として否定されています。
m: 比喩（地図）→本題（モデル）→結論の三段構成

t: 論旨：「誤った点で非現実的」の意味
p: A map that showed everything would be useless. To be of any help, a map must leave out almost all of what it represents—the individual trees, the colour of the doors, the people in the streets—and the choice of what to omit depends on the purpose for which it is made. A subway diagram that distorts distances beyond recognition may be the best possible guide for a passenger, and the worst possible guide for someone walking above ground. Scientific models work in much the same way. They are often criticised for being unrealistic, as though their simplifications were an embarrassing compromise. But a model's value lies precisely in what it ignores, provided that what it ignores does not matter for the question being asked. The proper objection to a model, then, is never simply that it is unrealistic, but that it is unrealistic in the wrong respects.
q: 最終文の unrealistic in the wrong respects が指す内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Simplifying or leaving out features that actually matter for the question the model is meant to answer.
Including so many details that the model becomes as complicated as reality itself.
Being criticised by people who do not understand the purpose of scientific models.
Failing to show features, such as trees and doors, that make a map look attractive.
e: 直前の文に provided that what it ignores does not matter for the question being asked（無視するものが問いにとって重要でない限り）とあります。裏返せば、問いにとって重要な点を無視・単純化していることが「誤った点で非現実的」ということです。細部を入れすぎることは逆の話です。批判者の無理解や地図の見た目の美しさは論点ではありません。
m: provided that＝〜という条件で

t: 文の挿入：翻訳できない語
p: It is often said that some words cannot be translated. [ 1 ] The Portuguese saudade, for instance, is regularly described as untranslatable, yet readers of English have no difficulty understanding a paragraph that explains it. What such claims usually mean is not that the meaning cannot be conveyed, but that it cannot be conveyed in a single word. [ 2 ] A language that lacks a term for a particular feeling does not leave its speakers incapable of having that feeling; it merely obliges them to describe it at greater length. Yet the length of a description is not a trivial matter. [ 3 ] What must be assembled from several words is less likely to be noticed, named, and passed on, and so it gradually recedes from the shared world of a community even if no individual is unable to grasp it.
q: 次の英文の空所［ 1 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: The claim is repeated so often that it has come to seem self-evident.
Concepts that are expensive to express tend to be expressed less often.
Translators, therefore, should avoid such words entirely.
This proves that speakers of different languages inhabit different worlds.
e: 空所の直後は The Portuguese saudade, for instance と「翻訳できないと言われる語」の例が続くので、空所には第1文の主張を受けてそれを話題として広げる文が入ります。「その主張はあまりに繰り返されて自明に見える」が自然です。2番目は第3段階（説明の長さが重要だ）の内容で、ここでは早すぎます。3番目の therefore は前に根拠がありません。4番目は「理解できない」方向の主張で、直後の「英語の読者は難なく理解する」と矛盾します。
m: 直後の for instance が何の例かを確認する

t: 文の挿入：翻訳できない語
p: It is often said that some words cannot be translated. [ 1 ] The Portuguese saudade, for instance, is regularly described as untranslatable, yet readers of English have no difficulty understanding a paragraph that explains it. What such claims usually mean is not that the meaning cannot be conveyed, but that it cannot be conveyed in a single word. [ 2 ] A language that lacks a term for a particular feeling does not leave its speakers incapable of having that feeling; it merely obliges them to describe it at greater length. Yet the length of a description is not a trivial matter. [ 3 ] What must be assembled from several words is less likely to be noticed, named, and passed on, and so it gradually recedes from the shared world of a community even if no individual is unable to grasp it.
q: 次の英文の空所［ 2 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: This distinction matters, because the two claims have very different implications.
Indeed, the feeling it names is unknown to anyone outside Portugal.
Dictionaries, after all, are written by people who know only one language.
This is why bilingual speakers often feel that they have two personalities.
e: 直前で「意味が伝えられない」ことと「一語では伝えられない」ことを区別し、直後で「語がなくても感情は持てる、長く説明する必要があるだけ」と、二つの主張の違いがもたらす帰結を述べています。したがって「この区別は重要だ、二つの主張の含意は大きく異なるから」が入ります。2番目は「英語の読者も理解できる」に反します。辞書の作り手やバイリンガルの性格は文脈と無関係です。
m: 空所の前後の「つなぎ役」になる文を選ぶ

m: Yet … not a trivial matter の理由を述べる文

t: 文の挿入：科学的知見の確立
p: Popular accounts of science tend to celebrate the moment of discovery: the experiment that worked, the insight that arrived in the bath. [ 1 ] Most published findings are not confirmed by any dramatic event at all; they simply survive, year after year, the attempts of other researchers to build on them. A result that cannot be reproduced does not collapse with a bang either. [ 2 ] Other laboratories try to use it, fail, and quietly turn to more promising lines of work, often without publishing their failures. This silent process is efficient in one sense, since it spares the field from endless public dispute. [ 3 ] Because unsuccessful attempts leave little trace, a newcomer may spend years pursuing a result that the most experienced researchers privately abandoned long ago.
q: 次の英文の空所［ 1 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: Such stories are memorable, but they misrepresent how knowledge is actually secured.
In another sense, however, it is remarkably wasteful.
Such stories explain why scientists rarely make mistakes.
Instead, it is slowly abandoned.
e: 直前は「発見の瞬間を称える通俗的な語り」、直後は「多くの知見は劇的な出来事ではなく、他の研究者の試みに耐えることで確かになる」です。両者をつなぐには「そうした話は記憶に残るが、知識が実際に確立される仕方を誤って伝えている」が適切です。2番目は「ある意味では効率的」の後でなければ意味をなしません。3番目は文脈にない主張です。4番目の Instead と it は前に受けるものがありません。
m: Such stories＝直前の「発見の物語」を受ける

e: 直前の efficient in one sense（ある意味では効率的）は、「別の意味では」という対比を予告しています。直後は「失敗の記録が残らないので新人が何年も無駄にする」と非効率の具体例です。したがって「しかし別の意味では、ひどく無駄が多い」が入ります。2番目は直後の問題点と矛盾します。3番目は「失敗を公表しないことが多い」に反します。4番目は第2空所の文です。
m: in one sense ↔ in another sense の対応

t: 文の挿入：退屈の効用
p: We tend to treat boredom as a problem to be eliminated, and modern life offers an endless supply of remedies. [ 1 ] Yet some psychologists suggest that boredom performs a useful function. It is, in their view, a signal that our current activity has ceased to engage us and that we ought to seek something more meaningful. [ 2 ] If every moment of potential tedium is immediately filled with a screen, the signal never has a chance to do its work. We do not feel bored, but neither are we prompted to ask what we would rather be doing. [ 3 ] The cure for boredom, in other words, may do more harm than the condition it relieves.
q: 次の英文の空所［ 1 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: A phone in the pocket guarantees that no queue or train journey need ever be dull.
As a result, boredom has become more common than ever before.
Like pain, it is unpleasant precisely so that we will not ignore it.
The discomfort disappears, and with it the question it was meant to raise.
e: 直前の「現代生活は退屈の対処法を無限に提供する」の具体例として「ポケットの携帯電話のおかげで、行列も電車の旅も退屈である必要がない」が入ります。2番目は「対処法が豊富」と矛盾します。3番目は「退屈には役割がある」という内容で、次の Yet（しかし役に立つと言う心理学者もいる）と対比になりません。4番目は信号が消える話で、まだ「信号」が出てきていない段階では早すぎます。
m: 具体例は抽象的な主張の直後に置く

t: 空所補充：都市と自然
p: Cities have long been imagined as the opposite of nature, places where the wild has been ( 1 ) in favour of the built. Ecologists who survey urban areas, however, increasingly find that cities harbour a surprising variety of species, some of which are rarely found in the surrounding countryside. Intensive agriculture has turned much of the rural landscape into what one might call a green desert: fields that look natural but are ( 2 ) to almost every species except the crop itself. By contrast, the disorderly patchwork of a city—abandoned lots, railway embankments, neglected gardens—offers a range of habitats that no efficient farmer would tolerate. None of this means that cities are good for nature ( 3 ); many species cannot survive in them at all. But it does suggest that the line between the urban and the natural is less sharp than we assume.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 1 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: pushed aside
carefully preserved
warmly celebrated
closely imitated
e: in favour of the built（人工物を優先して）とあるので、自然は「押しのけられた」と考えるのが自然です。都市を「自然の正反対」と見る従来の見方の説明でもあります。「大切に保存された」「温かく称えられた」は in favour of the built と矛盾します。「忠実に模倣された」も「自然の正反対」というイメージに合いません。
m: in favour of A＝Aを優先して（他を退けて）

m: be hostile to A＝Aにとって敵対的・不適な

m: without qualification＝無条件に・全面的に

t: 下線部の意味：専門家への信頼
p: Few of us can check the claims of a climate scientist or a cardiologist for ourselves, and so we must decide whom to trust without being able to judge what they say. This predicament is often presented as a weakness peculiar to modern democracy, but it is (1)【as old as the division of labour itself】. No farmer in a medieval village could assess the blacksmith's metallurgy; he could only observe whether the ploughs held. What has changed is not our dependence on others but (2)【the visibility of the seams】: we now see experts disagree in public, and we hear, often within the same hour, from people who merely sound like experts. Under these conditions, distrust is not necessarily a sign of ignorance. It may instead be (3)【a reasonable response to an unreasonable situation】, one in which the cues we once relied on—titles, institutions, a confident tone—can be imitated at almost no cost.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: The problem has existed ever since people began to specialize in different kinds of work.
The problem began when democracy divided citizens into competing parties.
The problem is a recent consequence of industrial mass production.
The problem can be solved by dividing labour more fairly among citizens.
e: as old as the division of labour itself は「分業そのものと同じくらい古い」、つまり人々が仕事を分担し専門化して以来ずっとある問題だという意味です。直後の中世の農民と鍛冶屋の例（農民は鍛冶の技術を評価できず、鋤が壊れないかを見るしかない）がこれを裏づけます。「民主主義」「近代の産業」に原因を求める選択肢は「近代特有ではない」という趣旨に反します。分業を公平にするという解決策は語られていません。
m: as old as A＝Aと同じくらい古い（Aの頃からある）

c: The points at which the system of expert knowledge visibly shows its divisions and weaknesses.
The boundaries between rich and poor citizens in modern societies.
The special clothing that once distinguished professionals from ordinary workers.
The formal rules that govern how public debates must be conducted.
e: seam は「縫い目・継ぎ目」で、ここでは専門知の体制の「ほころび・継ぎ目」の比喩です。コロンの後に「専門家が公の場で意見を対立させるのを目にし、専門家らしく聞こえるだけの人の話も聞く」と具体的に説明されています。つまり、かつては見えなかった専門知の分裂や弱点が見えるようになったということです。貧富の境界、職業の服装、討論の規則はいずれも本文と無関係です。
m: 比喩はコロン以下の説明で確かめる

Distrust makes sense because experts today are generally less competent than in the past.

Distrust makes sense because institutions have deliberately hidden their disagreements.
e: 下線部の後の one in which … can be imitated at almost no cost が「不合理な状況」の中身です。肩書き・組織・自信ある口調といった、かつて頼りにした手がかりがほとんどコストなしに真似できる状況では、不信は無知のしるしではなく合理的な反応だ、ということです。専門家の能力低下は書かれていません。一般の人が自分で確かめられないことは第1文の前提です。組織が意見の対立を隠したのではなく、むしろ公に見えるようになったのです。
m: one in which … が直前の名詞を説明する

t: 語句の意味：父の領収書
p: My father kept every receipt he had ever been given, filed by year in shoeboxes that (1)【colonized】 the top of his wardrobe and then, gradually, the spare room. When I was a teenager I thought this was simply what happened to men of his generation, a kind of (2)【harmless sediment】 left behind by decades of careful living. It was only after his death, sorting through the boxes with my sister, that I understood they were not records of money at all. On the back of a cinema ticket from 1974 he had written my mother's name, and the date, and nothing else. A bill from a seaside café carried a child's drawing of a crab—mine, my sister said, though I had no memory of it. We sat on the floor until the light went, (3)【reading our own lives back to ourselves in his handwriting】.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: gradually spread over and took up the space of
were neatly decorated with bright colours on
were removed one by one from
were carefully protected from the dust of
e: colonize は本来「植民地にする」ですが、ここでは靴箱が「洋服だんすの上を、さらに少しずつ空き部屋まで占領していった」という比喩です。then, gradually, the spare room と範囲が広がっていく様子からも「徐々に広がって場所を占めた」が適切です。装飾、取り除く、ほこりから守るはいずれも文脈に合いません。
m: colonize（比喩）＝じわじわ占領する

a valuable collection that could later be sold for money
a sign of mental illness that needed medical treatment
e: sediment は「沈殿物・堆積物」で、長い年月の間に自然にたまっていくものの比喩です。harmless（害のない）が付いているので「何年もかけて少しずつたまるが、特に害はないもの」となります。10代の語り手は、それを「父の世代の男性にありがちなこと」と軽く見ていたのです。健康を害する、売れる収集品、病気の兆候はいずれも harmless や語り手の当時の受け止め方に合いません。
m: sediment＝少しずつ積もるもの

t: 下線部の意味：父の領収書
p: My father kept every receipt he had ever been given, filed by year in shoeboxes that (1)【colonized】 the top of his wardrobe and then, gradually, the spare room. When I was a teenager I thought this was simply what happened to men of his generation, a kind of (2)【harmless sediment】 left behind by decades of careful living. It was only after his death, sorting through the boxes with my sister, that I understood they were not records of money at all. On the back of a cinema ticket from 1974 he had written my mother's name, and the date, and nothing else. A bill from a seaside café carried a child's drawing of a crab—mine, my sister said, though I had no memory of it. We sat on the floor until the light went, (3)【reading our own lives back to ourselves in his handwriting】.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: discovering, through the notes their father had left, how he had seen and treasured moments of their family life
reading aloud the letters that they had written to their father as children
checking whether their father's records of his spending had been accurate
writing down their own memories so that they would not be lost after his death
e: 語り手ときょうだいが見つけたのは、映画の半券の裏の母の名前と日付、海辺の食堂の勘定書に描かれた子どものカニの絵などでした。つまり領収書は「お金の記録ではまったくなかった」のです。下線部は「父の筆跡を通して、自分たち自身の人生を読み返していた」という意味で、父がどのように家族の時間を見て大切にしていたかを知ったということです。子どもの頃の手紙、支出の確認、自分たちで記録を書くことは本文にありません。
m: not records of money at all が読解の鍵

t: 語句の意味：孤独な天才像
p: We like to imagine that great works spring (1)【fully formed】 from the minds of their creators, and the romantic image of the solitary genius has proved remarkably durable. Historians of art and science, however, tend to (2)【take a dimmer view】 of it. Again and again they find that the same idea occurred to several people at about the same time, which suggests that the conditions for a discovery matter at least as much as the individual who happens to make it. This is not to deny that some people are more gifted than others. It is rather to say that talent, like a seed, (3)【needs the right soil】: without the instruments, the vocabulary, and the arguments of a particular moment, even the most brilliant mind would have nothing to work with.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: complete from the very beginning, without any process of gradual development
only after many years of patient revision
in a shape designed to suit public taste
as close copies of earlier works
e: spring fully formed from … は「〜から完成した姿で飛び出す」という意味で、制作の過程や時間を経ずに最初から完成している、というロマン主義的な天才像を表します。直後の the romantic image of the solitary genius（孤独な天才というロマン主義的イメージ）もそれを示します。「長年の推敲」はこの像と逆です。大衆の好み、先行作品の模倣はいずれも文脈にありません。
m: spring fully formed＝いきなり完成形で現れる

t: 語句の意味：孤独な天才像
p: We like to imagine that great works spring (1)【fully formed】 from the minds of their creators, and the romantic image of the solitary genius has proved remarkably durable. Historians of art and science, however, tend to (2)【take a dimmer view】 of it. Again and again they find that the same idea occurred to several people at about the same time, which suggests that the conditions for a discovery matter at least as much as the individual who happens to make it. This is not to deny that some people are more gifted than others. It is rather to say that talent, like a seed, (3)【needs the right soil】: without the instruments, the vocabulary, and the arguments of a particular moment, even the most brilliant mind would have nothing to work with.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: be more skeptical about
know less about
be more enthusiastic about
be confused by
e: take a dim view of A は「Aを好ましく思わない・懐疑的に見る」という慣用表現で、dimmer は比較級です。however（しかし）で「私たちが好む天才像」と対比され、続いて「同じ考えがほぼ同時に複数の人に浮かんだ例が繰り返し見つかる」と天才像を疑う根拠が示されます。「知識が少ない」「より熱心だ」は文脈と逆、「混乱している」は根拠がありません。
m: take a dim view of＝よく思わない

t: 下線部の意味：孤独な天才像
p: We like to imagine that great works spring (1)【fully formed】 from the minds of their creators, and the romantic image of the solitary genius has proved remarkably durable. Historians of art and science, however, tend to (2)【take a dimmer view】 of it. Again and again they find that the same idea occurred to several people at about the same time, which suggests that the conditions for a discovery matter at least as much as the individual who happens to make it. This is not to deny that some people are more gifted than others. It is rather to say that talent, like a seed, (3)【needs the right soil】: without the instruments, the vocabulary, and the arguments of a particular moment, even the most brilliant mind would have nothing to work with.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Individual ability can only bear fruit when the circumstances of the time supply what it requires.
Talent must be developed through physical labour such as farming.
Only people born in fertile regions can become great artists or scientists.
Gifted people should be separated from others so that their talent can grow.
e: 才能を種に、時代の条件を土にたとえています。コロン以下で「特定の時代の道具・語彙・議論がなければ、どんなに優れた頭脳も取り組む材料がない」と説明されているので、「個人の能力は、時代の状況が必要なものを与えるときに初めて実を結ぶ」が正解です。農作業、肥沃な地域、才能ある人の隔離はいずれも比喩を文字どおりに取ったり、本文と逆の方向に読んだりしたものです。
m: 比喩の「種」と「土」が何を指すかを対応させる

t: 下線部和訳：考える時間
p: (1)【It is not so much that we lack the time to think as that we have arranged our lives so as never to need it.】 Every gap in the day is filled before it can open, and every question that might have lingered is answered within seconds by a search. (2)【What would once have occupied an afternoon of puzzled reflection is now settled before we have properly understood what we were asking.】 The loss is hard to see, because nothing seems to be missing. (3)【Only when we find ourselves, by accident, without a signal do we notice how unaccustomed we have become to leaving a question open.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 私たちは考える時間がないというよりも、むしろ考える時間が決して必要にならないように生活を整えてしまったのだ。
私たちには考える時間がないので、考える必要が決して生じないように生活を整えてきたのだ。
考える時間が足りないことは、生活をうまく整えさえすれば決して問題にならない。
私たちは考える時間を持たず、それを必要としない生活を整えることもできていない。
e: It is not so much that A as that B は「AというよりむしろBなのだ」という構文です。A＝we lack the time to think、B＝we have arranged our lives so as never to need it（考える時間を決して必要としないように生活を整えた）。it は the time (to think) を指します。2番目は「AだからB」と因果関係に誤読しています。3番目は条件文として読み、4番目は両方を否定しており、いずれも構文を取り違えています。
m: not so much A as B＝AというよりむしろB

t: 下線部和訳：考える時間
p: (1)【It is not so much that we lack the time to think as that we have arranged our lives so as never to need it.】 Every gap in the day is filled before it can open, and every question that might have lingered is answered within seconds by a search. (2)【What would once have occupied an afternoon of puzzled reflection is now settled before we have properly understood what we were asking.】 The loss is hard to see, because nothing seems to be missing. (3)【Only when we find ourselves, by accident, without a signal do we notice how unaccustomed we have become to leaving a question open.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: かつてなら午後いっぱい頭を悩ませて考え込んだであろう事柄が、今では自分が何を問うていたのかをきちんと理解しないうちに片がついてしまう。
かつて午後いっぱい頭を悩ませた事柄も、今では何を問うべきかを理解した後で落ち着いて解決できるようになった。
午後に頭を悩ませて考えることは、自分が何を問うているかを理解するまでは決して落ち着かない。
かつて午後に考え込んだ人々は、今では自分の問いを理解する前に眠ってしまう。
e: What would once have occupied an afternoon of puzzled reflection が主語で、would have occupied は「（以前なら）〜を占めたであろう」という過去の推量です。is now settled は「今では決着がつく」、before we have properly understood what we were asking は「何を問うていたのかをきちんと理解しないうちに」です。2番目は before を「後で」と逆に訳しています。3番目は What 節を主語として読めていません。4番目の「眠ってしまう」は settle の誤訳です。
m: before＋完了形＝〜しないうちに

t: 下線部和訳：考える時間
p: (1)【It is not so much that we lack the time to think as that we have arranged our lives so as never to need it.】 Every gap in the day is filled before it can open, and every question that might have lingered is answered within seconds by a search. (2)【What would once have occupied an afternoon of puzzled reflection is now settled before we have properly understood what we were asking.】 The loss is hard to see, because nothing seems to be missing. (3)【Only when we find ourselves, by accident, without a signal do we notice how unaccustomed we have become to leaving a question open.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 偶然に電波の届かない状況に置かれて初めて、私たちは問いを未解決のままにしておくことにいかに不慣れになったかに気づく。
偶然に電波が届かなくなったときだけ、私たちは問いを開いたままにする習慣を身につける。
電波が届かないことに偶然気づくと、私たちはすぐに問いを解決しようとするようになる。
私たちは偶然に信号を見つけたときにだけ、問いを未解決のままにすることがいかに大切かに気づく。
e: Only when … do we notice は否定的な副詞句が文頭に出て倒置が起きた形で、「…して初めて〜に気づく」と訳します。without a signal は（携帯電話の）電波がない状態、how unaccustomed we have become to leaving a question open は「問いを開いたままにしておくことにいかに不慣れになってしまったか」です。2番目は notice を「身につける」と誤訳し、3番目は文意が逆です。4番目は without を読み落とし、unaccustomed を「大切」と誤っています。
m: Only when … do S V＝…して初めてSはVする

t: 誤り指摘：Hardly … when
p: The new rules on campus parking had been debated for months. (a)［Hardly had the committee］ (b)［announced its decision］ (c)［than protests began］ (d)［to spread among the students,］ (e)［forcing the president to reconsider.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) than protests began
(a) Hardly had the committee
(b) announced its decision
(d) to spread among the students,
(e) forcing the president to reconsider.
e: Hardly［Scarcely］ had S done … は when か before と組み合わせて「…するとすぐに」を表します。than と組むのは No sooner had S done … than の場合です。したがって(c)は when protests began とすべきです。(a)は否定の副詞 Hardly が文頭に出た倒置で正しく、(b)は過去分詞で had に続きます。(d) begin to do、(e)は結果を表す分詞構文で、いずれも正しい形です。
m: Hardly … when／No sooner … than の組を混同しない

t: 誤り指摘：主語と動詞の一致
p: Open science has become a central concern in many fields. The number of researchers (a)［who］ (b)［are willing to share their raw data］ (c)［have increased steadily,］ (d)［partly because funding agencies］ (e)［now require it.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) have increased steadily,
(a) who
(b) are willing to share their raw data
(d) partly because funding agencies
(e) now require it.
e: 主語は The number（数）で単数なので、動詞は has increased としなければなりません。of researchers who … に惑わされないことが大切です。(a)の who は researchers を先行詞とする関係代名詞、(b)の are は先行詞 researchers（複数）に一致しているので正しい形です。(d) partly because は「一つには〜だから」、(e)の require は主語 funding agencies（複数）に一致しています。
m: the number of＋複数名詞→単数扱い／a number of→複数扱い

t: 誤り指摘：関係詞の選択
p: My grandmother left her hometown more than sixty years ago. The village (a)［which she was born］ (b)［has changed so much that］ she (c)［barely recognizes it,］ (d)［though the old well］ (e)［still stands in the square.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (a) which she was born
(b) has changed so much that
(c) barely recognizes it,
(d) though the old well
(e) still stands in the square.
e: be born は自動詞の受動形で目的語を取らないため、関係代名詞 which だけでは関係節の中に入る場所がありません。where she was born または in which she was born とする必要があります。(b)は so … that 構文、(c) barely は「ほとんど〜ない」、(d) though は接続詞、(e) stand は「（建物などが）立っている」で、いずれも正しい用法です。
m: 関係節内に欠けた名詞がなければ関係副詞か前置詞＋which

t: 誤り指摘：look forward to＋動名詞
p: The discovery was announced at a press conference last week. Many scholars (a)［look forward to］ (b)［see the newly discovered letters,］ (c)［which are expected to］ (d)［shed light on］ the poet's (e)［final years.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (b) see the newly discovered letters,
(a) look forward to
(c) which are expected to
(d) shed light on
(e) final years.
e: look forward to の to は前置詞なので、後には名詞か動名詞が来ます。(b)は seeing the newly discovered letters としなければなりません。(c)の be expected to do は不定詞の to で、後の(d) shed light on（〜を解明する）は原形で正しい形です。which の先行詞は letters なので are も正しく、(e) final years も問題ありません。
m: look forward to / be used to / object to の to は前置詞

t: 誤り指摘：the＋比較級, the＋比較級
p: Historians have only recently gained access to the diaries of factory workers. (a)［The more closely we examine］ (b)［the historical record,］ (c)［more contradictions we discover］ (d)［between official accounts and］ (e)［what ordinary people wrote.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) more contradictions we discover
(a) The more closely we examine
(b) the historical record,
(d) between official accounts and
(e) what ordinary people wrote.
e: 「〜すればするほど…」は The＋比較級 …, the＋比較級 … の形で、後半にも the が必要です。(c)は the more contradictions we discover としなければなりません。(a)は前半として正しい形です。(b)は examine の目的語、(d) between A and B、(e)の what は関係代名詞で「普通の人々が書いたこと」となり、いずれも正しいです。
m: The＋比較級, the＋比較級（後半の the を落とさない）

t: 誤り指摘：不可算名詞
p: Writing a long essay for the first time can be overwhelming. The professor gave us (a)［several useful advices］ (b)［on how to］ (c)［organize a long essay,］ (d)［none of which I had］ (e)［thought of before.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (a) several useful advices
(b) on how to
(c) organize a long essay,
(d) none of which I had
(e) thought of before.
e: advice は不可算名詞なので複数形にできず、several とも結びつきません。several useful pieces of advice や some useful advice とします。(b) how to do は「〜の仕方」、(c)は原形で正しく、(d) none of which は前の内容を受ける非制限用法の関係代名詞、(e) think of は「〜を思いつく」で had thought は過去完了として正しい形です。
m: advice, information, furniture, news は数えない

t: 誤り指摘：one of＋複数名詞
p: The fall of ancient empires has been explained in many ways. Climate change is (a)［one of the most］ (b)［influential factor］ (c)［that historians have］ (d)［used to explain］ (e)［the decline of such empires.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (b) influential factor
(a) one of the most
(c) that historians have
(d) used to explain
(e) the decline of such empires.
e: one of the＋最上級＋名詞 では、名詞は複数形にします（「最も〜なものの一つ」）。(b)は influential factors とすべきです。(a)は正しい形です。(c) that は factors を先行詞とする関係代名詞で、(d) use A to do（Aを〜するのに用いる）の A が関係詞になっています。(e)も正しい名詞句です。
m: one of the＋最上級＋複数名詞

t: 誤り指摘：連鎖関係詞節の格
p: The award ceremony was held in Stockholm last December. The scientist (a)［whom many believe］ (b)［first identified the virus］ (c)［refused］ (d)［to accept any personal credit,］ (e)［insisting that it had been a team effort.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (a) whom many believe
(b) first identified the virus
(c) refused
(d) to accept any personal credit,
(e) insisting that it had been a team effort.
e: many believe の後に (that) S first identified the virus が続く形で、関係詞は identified の主語の役割をしています。したがって主格の who を使い、who many believe first identified the virus とします。(b)は関係節内の動詞句で正しく、(c) refuse to do、(d)の不定詞、(e)の付帯状況を表す分詞構文と、その中の過去完了も正しい形です。
m: S believe（挿入）の後に動詞→関係詞は主格 who

t: 誤り指摘：lie と lay
p: Exhausted after the long journey, she (a)［had laid on the sofa］ (b)［for nearly an hour］ (c)［before she noticed］ (d)［that someone］ (e)［had left a note on the table.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (a) had laid on the sofa
(b) for nearly an hour
(c) before she noticed
(d) that someone
(e) had left a note on the table.
e: 「横たわる」は自動詞 lie（lie–lay–lain）で、過去完了は had lain です。laid は他動詞 lay（横たえる）の過去・過去分詞で、目的語が必要です。(b) for nearly an hour は期間、(c)の before 節は過去形で「〜する前に」、(d) that 節、(e) had left は気づいた時点より前の出来事を表す過去完了で正しい形です。冒頭の Exhausted は分詞構文で、主語 she と一致しています。
m: lie–lay–lain（自）／lay–laid–laid（他）

t: 誤り指摘：enough の位置
p: The new hypothesis attracted wide attention when it was first proposed. However, it was (a)［not enough convincing］ (b)［to persuade those］ (c)［who had spent their careers］ (d)［studying the problem］ (e)［from another angle.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (a) not enough convincing
(b) to persuade those
(c) who had spent their careers
(d) studying the problem
(e) from another angle.
e: 副詞の enough は形容詞・副詞の後に置きます。(a)は not convincing enough としなければなりません（名詞を修飾する形容詞の enough は名詞の前に置けます）。(b) enough … to do の to 不定詞と those（人々）、(c)の関係代名詞 who、(d) spend A doing（Aを〜して過ごす）、(e) from another angle（別の角度から）はいずれも正しいです。
m: 形容詞＋enough to do（enough は後ろ）

t: 誤り指摘：Not only の倒置
p: The arrival of the railway transformed nineteenth-century Britain. (a)［Not only it changed］ (b)［the way people traveled,］ but the railway (c)［also altered］ (d)［how they thought about］ (e)［time itself.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (a) Not only it changed
(b) the way people traveled,
(c) also altered
(d) how they thought about
(e) time itself.

t: 誤り指摘：他動詞 mention
p: The lecture was part of a series on social history. In it, the historian (a)［mentioned about the role of］ (b)［women in the movement,］ (c)［a topic that］ (d)［had long been］ (e)［neglected by scholars.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (a) mentioned about the role of
(b) women in the movement,
(c) a topic that
(d) had long been
(e) neglected by scholars.

t: 物語：時計店の祖父
p:
The shop had been closing for eleven years. That, at least, was how my aunt put it: every January my grandfather announced that this would be the last year, and every December he renewed the lease. By the time I came to stay with him, the summer I turned fifteen, the window display had not been changed since before I was born, and most of the clocks on the walls had stopped at different hours, so that the room seemed to exist in several times at once.
I had expected to be bored, and for the first week I was. Customers were rare, and those who came seldom bought anything; they brought watches that had belonged to their parents and asked whether they could be made to run again. My grandfather would turn each one over in his fingers for a long time before answering. Often the answer was no. Once, after an elderly woman had left with her husband's watch still silent in her handbag, I asked him why he had not simply told her at once.
'Because she did not come to have it repaired,' he said. 'She came to be told that someone had tried.'
I thought this was the kind of thing old men say to make their failures sound wise. It was years later, standing in a hospital corridor with a doctor who took a long moment before speaking, that I understood what he had been giving those people, and how little it had cost him, and how much.
q: 本文の内容と一致するものを選びなさい。
c: Although the grandfather said every year that he would close the shop, he kept renewing the lease.
The narrator's aunt ran the shop together with the grandfather.
The clocks on the walls had been set to show the time in different cities.
Most customers came to the shop to buy new watches as presents.
e: 冒頭で「店は11年間閉店し続けていた」と逆説的に述べ、「毎年1月にこれが最後の年だと言い、毎年12月に賃貸契約を更新した」と説明しています。叔母はそう表現した（put it）だけで、店を手伝ってはいません。時計は「別々の時刻で止まっていた」のであって、各地の時刻に合わせたのではありません。客は親の形見の時計を持ち込み、めったに何も買わなかったと書かれています。
m: 冒頭の逆説（closing for eleven years）は直後で説明される

t: 物語：母の言語
p:
For most of my childhood, my mother's language was the one she used for the telephone. When her sister called from abroad, she would carry the receiver into the kitchen and close the door, and through the frosted glass I could hear her voice change—grow faster, louder, and somehow younger—in a way it never did when she spoke to us. I understood perhaps one word in twenty. I did not ask her to teach me, and she did not offer. It seemed to both of us, I think, that the language belonged to a life she had left behind, and that to bring it into our house would be to admit how much of her remained there.
At university I enrolled in an evening course, telling no one. The teacher was a young man who had grown up in the same city as my mother, and when he corrected my pronunciation he would sometimes laugh and say that I sounded like somebody's grandmother. I did not tell him why.
The first time I spoke to my mother in her own language, she was peeling potatoes at the sink. I said only that the soup smelled good. She did not turn round. For a long moment the only sound was the knife against the potato, and I began to fear that I had made a terrible mistake. Then she answered me—slowly, the way one speaks to a child—and asked who had taught me to talk like her mother.
q: 語り手が母親に言語を教えてほしいと頼まなかった理由として、本文から読み取れる最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Both of them seemed to feel that the language belonged to the mother's past, and bringing it home would reveal how strongly she was still tied to that past.
The mother had told the narrator that the language was too difficult for a child to learn.
The narrator was not interested in the language until a university teacher encouraged that interest.
The narrator thought that the language was useful only for telephone calls with relatives.
e: 第1段落最終文に「その言語は母が後にしてきた人生に属し、家に持ち込むことは、母のどれほど多くの部分がまだそこにあるかを認めることになると、二人とも感じていた」とあります。母が「難しすぎる」と言った記述はありません。語り手は自分から誰にも言わずに夜間講座に入ったので、教師に勧められたのではありません。「電話でしか役に立たない」は、語り手が言語を使う場面を述べただけで、頼まなかった理由ではありません。
m: It seemed to both of us … that 〜 が理由の核心

t: 評論：数値による管理
p:
Organisations increasingly manage what they can measure, and there is much to be said for this. Numbers allow comparisons across time and place, expose favouritism, and make it harder for the powerful to hide their failures behind vague assurances. A hospital that reports its waiting times can be held to account in a way that one which merely promises to care for its patients cannot.
Yet the very features that make numbers useful also make them dangerous. A measure is chosen because it is thought to track something we value but cannot observe directly—the quality of care, say, or what students actually know. Once people are rewarded or punished according to that measure, however, they have every reason to improve the number by whatever means are cheapest, and the cheapest means seldom coincide with improving the thing itself. Teachers drill pupils in the format of examinations; hospitals reclassify patients so that they no longer count as waiting. The indicator rises while the reality it was meant to indicate stays where it was, or declines.
The usual response is to devise better measures, and sometimes this helps. But it cannot solve the underlying problem, which is not technical but a matter of attention. Any figure, however sophisticated, captures only part of what matters, and the more weight we place on it, the more we invite people to neglect the rest. The alternative is not to abandon measurement but to treat numbers as questions rather than verdicts—as prompts to go and look, instead of substitutes for looking.
q: 筆者によれば、数値が「危険」になるのはなぜか。最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: When rewards depend on a measure, people tend to raise the figure by the easiest route rather than by improving what it was meant to reflect.
Numbers are usually calculated incorrectly by organisations that lack technical experts.
Numbers make it impossible to compare institutions across time and place.
Powerful people use numbers to hide their failures behind vague assurances.
e: 第2段落で「数値に応じて賞罰が与えられると、人は最も安上がりな方法で数値を上げようとし、その方法は対象そのものの改善とめったに一致しない」と述べ、試験形式の反復練習や患者の分類変更を例に挙げています。計算の誤りは論点ではありません。比較を可能にすることは数値の利点として挙げられています。4番目は逆で、数値は「曖昧な約束の陰に失敗を隠すこと」を難しくするとされています。
m: 指標が目標になると、指標と実態がずれる

t: 評論：忘却とデジタル記録
p:
For most of human history, information was lost unless someone made an effort to keep it. Records had to be written by hand, copied, stored, and protected from fire and damp, and only what someone judged worth the trouble survived. Today the relationship has been reversed. Digital storage is so cheap that it is easier to keep everything than to decide what to discard, and so our messages, photographs, and casual remarks accumulate without anyone having chosen to preserve them.
It is tempting to see this as pure gain. Historians of the future, after all, will know far more about our daily lives than we know about those of our ancestors. But individuals and societies have always relied on forgetting as much as on memory. A person who could never forget an insult would find forgiveness almost impossible; a community that kept every youthful mistake permanently on display would leave little room for anyone to become someone different. Forgetting, in this sense, is not merely a failure of storage but a condition of change.
Some legal systems have begun to recognise a right to have certain information removed from public view after a period of time. Critics object that this amounts to rewriting history, and the concern is not frivolous. Yet the purpose of such rules is not to make the past disappear but to restore something like the gradual fading that once happened of its own accord—to let the past remain available to those with a reason to seek it, without forcing it on everyone else.
q: 本文中の Today the relationship has been reversed. の内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Whereas preserving records once required deliberate effort, it is now discarding them that requires a conscious decision.
Whereas people once forgot easily, they now have much better natural memories.
Whereas records were once cheap to keep, they are now extremely expensive to store.
Whereas historians once knew everything about daily life, they now know very little.
e: 第1文で「かつては誰かが労力をかけて残さない限り、情報は失われた」とあり、「関係が逆転した」とはこれが逆になったことです。直後に「保存が安いので、何を捨てるか決めるより全部とっておくほうが楽」とあり、今では「残す」ではなく「捨てる」ほうに判断と労力がいる、ということです。人の記憶力の向上の話ではありません。保存のコストは逆に安くなりました。歴史家の知識の比較は未来についての話で、内容も逆です。
m: reversed は直前の文と対比して読む

For most of human history, information was lost unless someone made an effort to keep it. Records had to be written by hand, copied, stored, and protected from fire and damp, and only what someone judged worth the trouble survived. Today the relationship has been reversed. Digital storage is so cheap that it is easier to keep everything than to decide what to discard, and so our messages, photographs, and casual remarks accumulate without anyone having chosen to preserve them.
It is tempting to see this as pure gain. Historians of the future, after all, will know far more about our daily lives than we know about those of our ancestors. But individuals and societies have always relied on forgetting as much as on memory. A person who could never forget an insult would find forgiveness almost impossible; a community that kept every youthful mistake permanently on display would leave little room for anyone to become someone different. Forgetting, in this sense, is not merely a failure of storage but a condition of change.
Some legal systems have begun to recognise a right to have certain information removed from public view after a period of time. Critics object that this amounts to rewriting history, and the concern is not frivolous. Yet the purpose of such rules is not to make the past disappear but to restore something like the gradual fading that once happened of its own accord—to let the past remain available to those with a reason to seek it, without forcing it on everyone else.
q: 情報の削除を求める権利について、筆者の考えとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: It aims to recreate the natural fading of information while keeping the past available to those with a genuine reason to look for it.
It should be rejected, because any removal of information amounts to rewriting history.
It ensures that unpleasant parts of the past are permanently erased from all records.
The critics' objection to it is completely groundless and should be ignored.
e: 最終文に「こうした規則の目的は過去を消すことではなく、かつて自然に起きていた緩やかな風化に近いものを取り戻すこと、すなわち理由のある人には過去を利用可能にしたまま、それを他の全員に押しつけないことだ」とあります。筆者は批判を the concern is not frivolous（軽く扱える懸念ではない）と認めたうえで Yet と反論しているので、2番目の全面否定も4番目の「根拠がない」も誤りです。3番目は not to make the past disappear に反します。
m: 譲歩（not frivolous）＋ Yet＝筆者の本音

t: 要約：睡眠と記憶の定着
p: Most students know the experience of struggling with a problem late at night, giving up, and finding the solution obvious the next morning. Folk wisdom calls this 'sleeping on it', and laboratory studies suggest that the phrase is more than a figure of speech. During sleep the brain does not simply switch off; it replays the day's experiences and strengthens some connections while letting others fade. Importantly, this process seems to favour what is likely to be useful later over what was merely vivid at the time. It would be a mistake, however, to conclude that sleep can replace study. Material that was never learned cannot be consolidated, and a night's rest merely sorts what is already there. Sleep is therefore best understood not as a shortcut but as the second half of learning, the part that takes place when we are no longer trying.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 睡眠中に脳は日中の経験を再生して後で役立ちそうなものを定着させるが、それは学習の代わりにはならず、努力して学んだ後に続く学習の後半部分である。
睡眠中に脳は鮮明だった記憶を優先して強め、役に立たない記憶を消すので、徹夜で勉強するより十分に眠るほうが確実に成績が上がる。
脳は睡眠中も活動しているので、眠る前に十分に勉強していなくても、睡眠さえとれば解けなかった問題が翌朝にはひとりでに解けるようになる。
「寝て考える」という言い伝えは実験では裏づけられておらず、睡眠と学習の関係は単なる比喩として語られているだけで、実際の効果はごく小さいと考えるべきである。
e: 本文は、①睡眠中に脳が経験を再生し、後で役立つものを強める、②だが学んでいないことは定着しない、③だから睡眠は学習の近道ではなく「後半部分」だ、という流れです。2番目は「鮮明なもの優先」が本文と逆、3番目は睡眠が学習の代わりになるという誤り、4番目は実験が比喩以上だと示しているという本文に反します。
m: 要約は「現象→仕組み→注意→結論」の順にたどる

c: Because it works on what has already been learned, sorting and strengthening it after the studying is over.
Because it allows students to take in new material without any effort at all while they are unconscious.

q: 本文中の Material that was never learned cannot be consolidated という文の役割として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: It gives the reason why sleep cannot be a substitute for study.
It offers a counterexample to the claim that the brain replays the day.
It introduces a new experiment that contradicts the earlier findings.
It restates the folk wisdom mentioned at the beginning of the passage.
e: 直前の It would be a mistake … to conclude that sleep can replace study（睡眠が勉強の代わりになるとは言えない）の理由を述べる文です。学んでいないものは定着させようがない、という根拠になっています。2番目の「反例」は、脳が経験を再生するという主張を否定しておらず誤り。3番目は実験の紹介ではなく、4番目は冒頭の言い伝えの言い換えでもありません。
m: 直前の主張の「理由」になる文かを確かめる

t: 要約：図書館と社会的基盤
p: Public libraries are usually defended as places to borrow books, and by that measure they seem to be in decline, since in many cities the number of loans has fallen for years. Yet visitors have not stopped coming. They come to use computers, to attend language classes, to sit warmly through a winter afternoon, or simply to be among others without being expected to buy anything. Sociologists who study such places call them 'social infrastructure': not buildings that serve a single function, but settings that make casual contact between different kinds of people possible. The distinction matters for policy. If a library is judged only by its circulation figures, a council may close it as unnecessary; if it is understood as infrastructure, its value lies in what it quietly prevents: isolation, and the hardening of boundaries between groups who would otherwise never meet.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 図書館は貸出数では衰退して見えるが、本以外の目的でも人が集まり、多様な人が自然に接する「社会的基盤」として働いており、貸出数だけで測ると価値を見誤る。
図書館の貸出数が減り続けているのは利用者が電子書籍へ移ったためなので、自治体は図書館の閉鎖を進め、その分の予算を電子図書の整備に回すことが望ましい。
図書館は語学教室やコンピュータの提供など貸出以外の事業を広げたので、貸出数が減っても利用者数は以前よりずっと増えているとされる。
社会学者は図書館を単一の機能を持つ建物として定義しており、その機能が弱まった以上、政策として存続を支える根拠は乏しいと結論づけている。
e: 本文は、貸出数は減ったが人は来続けている→図書館は多様な人の接触を生む「社会的基盤」→貸出数だけで評価すると閉鎖の根拠になりかねない、という展開です。2番目は電子書籍が本文にありません。3番目は「利用者が増えた」と言っていません（stopped coming ではない）。4番目は社会学者の定義と逆（単一機能ではない）です。
m: 数字で測れない価値は「何を防ぐか」で考える

t: 論旨：測り方が政策を左右する

q: 本文の The distinction matters for policy. の理由として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Whether a library is kept open may depend on whether it is measured by loans or by the contact it makes possible.
Policy makers have so far ignored the sociologists' definition of social infrastructure when deciding which libraries to close.
Circulation figures cannot be collected in places where people do not borrow books, so councils have no figures to judge them by.
Councils should spend more on computers and language classes than on books, because books are no longer borrowed by anyone.
e: The distinction は「貸出の場」と「社会的基盤」という見方の違いです。続く文が、貸出数だけで判断すれば閉鎖されうるが、基盤と見れば価値が別にある、と説明しています。2番目の「政策担当者が無視してきた」は本文にありません。3番目は数字が集められないとは述べておらず、4番目の予算配分の提案も本文にありません。
m: The distinction の指す内容を直前の文で確認する

t: 論旨：図書館が防ぐもの
p: Public libraries are usually defended as places to borrow books, and by that measure they seem to be in decline, since in many cities the number of loans has fallen for years. Yet visitors have not stopped coming. They come to use computers, to attend language classes, to sit warmly through a winter afternoon, or simply to be among others without being expected to buy anything. Sociologists who study such places call them 'social infrastructure': not buildings that serve a single function, but settings that make casual contact between different kinds of people possible. The distinction matters for policy. If a library is judged only by its circulation figures, a council may close it as unnecessary; if it is understood as infrastructure, its value lies in what it quietly prevents: isolation, and the hardening of boundaries between groups who would otherwise never meet.
q: 筆者が、図書館の価値は what it quietly prevents にあると述べるときの「防ぐもの」として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Isolation and the hardening of boundaries between groups
A fall in the number of books that are borrowed each year
The closure of old buildings that serve only one function
Competition among local councils for limited public money
e: コロン以下に isolation, and the hardening of boundaries between groups who would otherwise never meet とあります。2番目の貸出数の減少は、むしろ図書館が衰退して見える理由で、防がれるものではありません。3番目・4番目は本文に根拠がありません。
m: コロン（:）の後ろは直前の語句の具体的な言い換え

t: 要約：鉄道と標準時
p: Until the nineteenth century, every town kept its own time, set by the sun at noon. This caused little trouble so long as travel was slow; a traveller who went from one town to another simply adjusted his watch. The railways changed this. A timetable that listed dozens of stations was useless if each station's clock disagreed with the next, and accidents on single tracks made the disagreement dangerous. Railway companies therefore introduced a common time, and governments later made it law. It is tempting to describe this as the triumph of reason over local habit, but the story is more complicated. Many people resisted, arguing that 'railway time' was an insult to nature. Their objection was not foolish: they understood that when time is no longer read from the sky, it becomes something that can be imposed from a distance, and so a matter of authority rather than observation.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 鉄道の普及で町ごとの時刻が統一されたが、それは単なる合理化ではなく、時間が観測ではなく遠くから課される権威の問題になる変化でもあり、抵抗にも理由があった。
鉄道会社が共通の時刻を導入したのは事故を防ぐためだけであって、時刻の統一に反対した人々の主張には、初めから何の根拠もなく、すぐに忘れ去られた。
時刻の統一は、町ごとの太陽時を守ろうとした人々の努力が実り、最終的には政府ではなく鉄道会社の主導で法制化まで進んだと考えられている。
旅行が遅かった時代の人々は時計を調整する習慣そのものがなく、鉄道によって初めて、時計を正確に合わせる必要があることを知った。
e: 本文は、町ごとの太陽時→鉄道の時刻表と事故防止のため共通時刻→これを「理性の勝利」と単純には言えない→反対者は、時間が空から読むものでなくなると権威が課すものになると理解していた、という流れです。2番目は反対に根拠がないとして本文の not foolish に反し、3番目は経緯が逆で、4番目は本文にない内容です。
m: 「単純な勝利物語ではない」という筆者の留保をつかむ

t: 論旨：反対者は愚かではない
p: Until the nineteenth century, every town kept its own time, set by the sun at noon. This caused little trouble so long as travel was slow; a traveller who went from one town to another simply adjusted his watch. The railways changed this. A timetable that listed dozens of stations was useless if each station's clock disagreed with the next, and accidents on single tracks made the disagreement dangerous. Railway companies therefore introduced a common time, and governments later made it law. It is tempting to describe this as the triumph of reason over local habit, but the story is more complicated. q: 本文の Their objection was not foolish の理由として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: They saw that standardised time shifts the source of time from natural observation to a distant authority.
They correctly predicted that railway accidents would increase on single tracks in the end.
They had worked out that local sun time was more accurate than the clock time of the railways.
They knew that governments had no power to make a common time into law at any time.
e: 理由はコロン以下の they understood that … に書かれています。時間が空（太陽）から読み取られなくなると、遠くから課される権威の問題になる、という洞察です。2番目の事故の予測、3番目の太陽時のほうが正確という主張、4番目の政府に権限がないという認識は、いずれも本文に述べられていません。
m: not foolish の直後のコロンに理由が書かれる

t: 論旨：理性対習慣という図式
p: Until the nineteenth century, every town kept its own time, set by the sun at noon. This caused little trouble so long as travel was slow; a traveller who went from one town to another simply adjusted his watch. The railways changed this. A timetable that listed dozens of stations was useless if each station's clock disagreed with the next, and accidents on single tracks made the disagreement dangerous. Railway companies therefore introduced a common time, and governments later made it law. It is tempting to describe this as the triumph of reason over local habit, but the story is more complicated. Many people resisted, arguing that 'railway time' was an insult to nature. Their objection was not foolish: they understood that when time is no longer read from the sky, it becomes something that can be imposed from a distance, and so a matter of authority rather than observation.
q: It is tempting to describe this as the triumph of reason over local habit, but the story is more complicated. に表れる筆者の態度として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: The author accepts the benefits of a common time but thinks the simple story of reason against habit hides something important.
The author regards the introduction of railway time as a mistake that ought to have been reversed.
The author agrees that the resistance was merely a sentimental attachment to old habits.
The author argues that accidents were the only real cause of the change.
e: but 以下で「話はもっと複雑だ」と述べ、後半で反対者の洞察を認めています。つまり利点を否定せず、単純な図式を退けています。2番目は「誤りだった」とまで言っておらず、3番目は反対を感傷と片づけており本文に反し、4番目は事故が「唯一の原因」と限定している点が誤りです。
m: It is tempting to … but ～は「単純化への留保」の型

t: 要約：市民による野鳥観察
p: Every spring, thousands of amateur birdwatchers record what they see in their gardens and parks and upload their lists to a shared database. Professional ornithologists, who once regarded such enthusiasts with some suspicion, now rely on them. The reason is scale. No team of scientists could afford to be in ten thousand places at once, but ten thousand volunteers, each in a different place, can reveal changes in the range of a species that would otherwise go unnoticed for decades. The method has weaknesses, of course. Volunteers watch where it is pleasant to watch, so that gardens are overrepresented and remote moorland is almost absent, and an unusual bird is far more likely to be reported than a common one. Careful analysts therefore do not treat the raw lists as a picture of nature; they treat them as a picture of nature seen through human habits, and they correct for those habits. In this way the limits of the data become part of the science rather than a reason to reject it.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 市民の野鳥観察記録は、多数の場所を同時に観察できる規模の点で専門家に欠かせないが、人の行動による偏りがあるので、補正して分析に組み込む必要がある。
アマチュアの観察記録には誤りが多いため、専門家は自ら現地へ出向いて同じ調査をやり直し、市民の記録は検証のための参考資料としてしか用いていない。
市民の観察者は庭や公園を好むのでデータは都市の鳥の分布しか示さず、遠隔地の鳥の変化を知る手段は今のところまったく存在しない。
珍しい鳥ほど報告されやすいという偏りがあるので、観察記録を共有するデータベースは専門家の間で次第に使われなくなっている。
e: 本文は、専門家が市民の記録に頼る理由（規模）→偏りという弱点→偏りを補正して分析することで限界がかえって科学の一部になる、という構成です。2番目は専門家が今は頼っているという本文に反し、3番目は「手段が皆無」と言い過ぎで、4番目は使われなくなっているという記述がありません。
m: 長所→弱点→それを逆手に取る、の三段をたどる

q: 本文の The reason is scale. の説明として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Many volunteers in different places can show changes that a small team of scientists could not detect.
Volunteers are better trained than professional ornithologists at identifying rare species of birds, especially in spring.
Volunteers work without payment, which greatly lowers the cost of every research project.
Amateurs prefer remote moorland, where professionals only seldom go to carry out their work, so they cover the most unusual places.

m: scale＝規模。直後の説明文が答えになる

t: 論旨：データの限界が科学の一部に
p: Every spring, thousands of amateur birdwatchers record what they see in their gardens and parks and upload their lists to a shared database. Professional ornithologists, who once regarded such enthusiasts with some suspicion, now rely on them. The reason is scale. No team of scientists could afford to be in ten thousand places at once, but ten thousand volunteers, each in a different place, can reveal changes in the range of a species that would otherwise go unnoticed for decades. Volunteers watch where it is pleasant to watch, so that gardens are overrepresented and remote moorland is almost absent, and an unusual bird is far more likely to be reported than a common one. q: 本文最後の the limits of the data become part of the science の意味として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Knowing the biases of the data is itself used in the analysis, instead of being a reason to throw it away.
Scientists have decided that incomplete data should never be published in journals.
The weaknesses have been removed by asking volunteers to watch more remote places.
Because the data are imperfect, analysts treat them as a picture of nature that has no human influence at all.
e: 直前に、分析者は生の記録を「人間の習慣を通して見た自然」と捉え、その習慣を補正すると書かれています。偏りを知ること自体が分析の一部になる、という意味です。2番目は発表しないという話ではなく、3番目は観察地を変えて弱点を除いたとは述べておらず、4番目は人間の影響を「ない」としており本文と逆です。
m: 偏りは捨てずに「補正する」材料にする

t: 要約：降水確率の読み方
p: When a forecaster says there is a thirty per cent chance of rain, many listeners assume the forecaster is hedging, as though a confident forecaster would simply say yes or no. In fact the figure carries information that a yes or no cannot. It says that, on days with conditions like tomorrow's, it has rained on roughly three days out of ten. A forecaster whose thirty per cent days are followed by rain about thirty per cent of the time is, in a precise sense, correct, even though on any particular day it either rains or it does not. This is hard to accept, because we are used to judging predictions by single outcomes. We remember the picnic ruined by a 'ten per cent' shower and forget the many dry afternoons that the same figure correctly foretold. To read a probability well is to give up the wish to be told what will happen, and to settle for being told how much to expect it.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 降水確率の数字は曖昧さの表れではなく、似た条件の日に実際に雨が降る割合を示す情報であり、単発の結果で当たり外れを判断してはならない。

m: 確率は「頻度の情報」。1回の結果で正誤を決めない

t: 論旨：確率が「正しい」と言える理由
p: When a forecaster says there is a thirty per cent chance of rain, many listeners assume the forecaster is hedging, as though a confident forecaster would simply say yes or no. In fact the figure carries information that a yes or no cannot. It says that, on days with conditions like tomorrow's, it has rained on roughly three days out of ten. A forecaster whose thirty per cent days are followed by rain about thirty per cent of the time is, in a precise sense, correct, even though on any particular day it either rains or it does not. This is hard to accept, because we are used to judging predictions by single outcomes. We remember the picnic ruined by a 'ten per cent' shower and forget the many dry afternoons that the same figure correctly foretold. To read a probability well is to give up the wish to be told what will happen, and to settle for being told how much to expect it.
q: 本文の A forecaster … is, in a precise sense, correct の理由として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: The frequency of rain on such days matches the stated figure, whatever happens on one particular day.
It rains on thirty days of every hundred in the forecaster's country, taking all the seasons together.
The forecaster always warns listeners to carry an umbrella whenever the figure is above zero.
Listeners remember the dry afternoons more clearly than they remember the ruined picnics.
e: 「三割と言った日のうち、実際に雨が降るのが約三割」であれば、数字は頻度として正確だ、というのが本文の考えです。ある一日に降るか降らないかとは別の水準の話です。2番目は国全体の雨の日数の話で、3番目と4番目は本文にない内容です（4番目は本文の We remember the picnic ruined と逆）。
m: 確率の正しさは「同じ条件の日の長期的な割合」で測る

t: 要約：言葉の乱れという不満
p: Every generation of adults seems to believe that the young are ruining their language. Complaints about slang, about new words and about shifting grammar can be found in writings from many centuries ago, and the pattern is so regular that it deserves an explanation. One is simply that we notice what is unfamiliar. The words we learned in childhood feel like the language itself, while those that appear later feel like additions, however useful they may become. Another is that language is tied to social standing, so that disapproval of a new usage is often disapproval of the people who use it. Linguists do not conclude from this that anything goes. Clarity matters, and a form that confuses listeners tends, in the long run, to be abandoned. But they point out that the forms later generations accept as correct are often the very forms an earlier generation condemned, and this should make us hesitate before treating our own preferences as laws.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 言葉が乱れているという不満は世代を越えて繰り返され、見慣れない形への違和感や評価が背景にあり、後世に正しいとされる形が過去に非難された例も多いので、自分の好みを絶対視すべきではない。
新しい言い回しは聞き手を混乱させない限りいつの間にか定着していくので、言語学者は文法や語法に守るべき決まりは必要ないと主張している。
若者の言葉づかいへの不満は昔にはなく、インターネットが普及した近年になって初めて目立つようになった新しい現象であり、過去の文献にはそのような不満はほとんど見当たらない。
言語の変化に対する批判は社会的地位の高い人々の言葉を守る役割を果たしてきたので、言語学者はそのような批判を正当なものとして広く認めている。
e: 本文の骨格は、①言葉の乱れへの不満は昔から繰り返される、②理由は見慣れなさと社会的評価、③明瞭さは大事だが、後世に正用とされる形が過去に非難された例が多い、④だから自分の好みを法則と見なすのは慎重に、です。2番目は anything goes を否定する本文に反し、3番目は昔からあるという本文と逆、4番目は批判を正当化する話ではありません。
m: 「不満は昔から」→「理由」→「だから慎重に」の順にまとめる

t: 要約：美術館での鑑賞時間
p: Studies of museum visitors have found that people spend, on average, less than half a minute in front of a famous painting, and a good part of that time is spent reading the label or taking a photograph. The finding is usually reported as a sign of shallow engagement, a symptom of an age of distraction. It may, however, say as much about museums as about visitors. A gallery crowded with hundreds of works invites us to treat each as an item on a list, and a visitor who has travelled far to see a collection feels obliged to see all of it. Some museums have therefore begun to experiment with showing fewer works, or with asking visitors to look at a single picture for ten minutes before reading anything about it. Participants often report that the picture changes: details emerge, the first impression is revised, and the work seems to become less famous and more particular. Looking, it turns out, is a skill that depends on being given time, and the conditions for it can be designed.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 来館者が名画の前で過ごす時間の短さは気の散りやすさだけでなく展示の作りにも原因があり、作品数を絞ったり長く見る機会を設けたりすれば、鑑賞は時間を与えられて育つ技能として変わりうる。
美術館の来館者は名画の前でラベルを読んだり写真を撮ったりすることに時間をかけすぎるので、解説文を減らして撮影を禁じれば、鑑賞時間は自然に長くなると考えられる。
美術館が展示作品を減らした結果、来館者は遠くから訪れる意味を感じなくなり、全体の来館者数が急速に減ってしまった。

t: 要約：贈与と売買
p: A gift is supposed to be free, yet anyone who has received one knows that it is rarely free of consequences. Anthropologists observed long ago that in many societies gifts create obligations: the receiver must give something back, not at once, since an immediate return would look like payment, but eventually and in a form that shows respect. The system looks inefficient, since the same value could be exchanged more simply through a sale. Its point, however, is precisely what a sale avoids. A purchase ends the relationship between buyer and seller; each leaves with what they wanted and owes the other nothing. A gift keeps the parties in debt to each other, and it is this continuing debt that binds them together. When we complain that modern life has made our dealings impersonal, we may be describing nothing more mysterious than the replacement of gifts by sales.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 贈り物は返礼の義務を生み、続く貸し借りが人々を結びつけるが、売買は取引が終われば貸し借りが残らないので、現代の人間関係の希薄さは贈与が売買に置き換わった結果とも考えられる。
贈り物にはその場ですぐ返礼する習慣があり、釣り合う価値を返すことで、双方の負担を軽くして関係を円滑に保っている。
売買は贈り物よりも効率的で公平な交換の方法であり、人類学者は、贈与の制度は非効率なので社会から消えていくと考えている。
贈り物を受け取った人は返礼の義務を負うが、その義務が人間関係を重苦しくするので、現代社会では贈与を避けて、貸し借りの残らない売買を選ぶ人が増えたと人類学者は結論づけている。
e: 本文は、贈り物は返礼の義務を生む→売買は関係を終わらせるが、贈与は続く負債で人を結びつける→現代の非人格的な関係は贈与が売買に置き換わった結果かもしれない、という論旨です。2番目は即時の返礼を否定する本文に反し、3番目は消えるという記述がなく、4番目は因果が本文と異なります。
m: 贈与＝続く負債が絆になる。売買＝貸し借りなし

t: 要約：海底の地図と月面
p: We often hear that more is known about the surface of the Moon than about the floor of the ocean. The comparison is slightly unfair, since the Moon can be photographed from above, whereas seawater absorbs light and radio waves so quickly that the sea floor cannot be seen from space. Scientists have to rely on sound, sending pulses from ships and timing their echoes, a method which is accurate but slow, since a ship can survey only a narrow strip at a time. As a result, large areas of the deep ocean have been mapped at a resolution coarser than that of maps of other planets. The point of the comparison, then, is not that scientists have been lazy but that the obstacles differ in kind: what is hard about the ocean is not distance but the medium that lies in the way.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 海底の地図が月面より粗いのは研究者の怠慢ではなく、海水が光や電波を通さず音による調査に頼るしかないという媒体の性質のためである。
月は上空から撮影できるが海は撮影できないため、科学者は月の探査を優先するようになり、海底の調査にはほとんど予算を回さなくなり、地図の改良は止まった。
音を使った海底調査は精度が低いので、ほかの惑星の地図よりも粗い地図しか作れず、改善の見込みもまったく立っていないと説明されている。
月面より海底のほうが遠くにあり、距離が調査を妨げているので、船を増やせば短期間のうちに詳細な地図を作ることができる。
e: 本文は、海水は光や電波を吸収するので宇宙から見えない→音で調べるが一度に狭い帯しか調べられない→困難は距離ではなく間にある媒体にある、という流れです。2番目は予算配分の話が本文にありません。3番目は音の方法を accurate（正確）としており、4番目は not distance と述べる本文に反します。
m: 困難の「種類」が違う、という結論を押さえる

t: 要約：受け入れられる謝罪
p: A public apology is easy to criticise. If it comes too early, it seems to be a way of ending the discussion before anyone has understood what happened; if it comes late, it looks forced. Yet the apologies that people accept have a pattern. They name the specific wrong instead of speaking vaguely of 'any offence that may have been caused'. They do not shift attention to the apologiser's own suffering. And they are followed by some action that costs something, since words that cost nothing are easily doubted. These features suggest that an apology is not mainly an expression of feeling. It is a kind of promise, whose sincerity is judged by what the speaker is prepared to give up.
q: 次の英文の内容を日本語で要約したものとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 謝罪が受け入れられるのは、誤りを具体的に述べ、自分の苦痛に話をすり替えず、代償を伴う行動が続く場合であり、謝罪は感情の表現というより、何かを手放す覚悟を示す約束である。
謝罪は早すぎれば議論を終わらせるためと疑われ、遅すぎれば強制されたと見られるので、最も適切な時期は事件の直後から数日後である。
公の謝罪では気持ちを正直に表すことが何より大切で、具体的な誤りを挙げることよりも、自分がどれほど苦しんだかを率直に語る謝罪のほうが、人々に受け入れられやすい。
謝罪の言葉は代償を伴わなくても信用されるが、曖昧な表現を避けて被害を具体的に述べることが唯一の条件である。
e: 本文は、受け入れられる謝罪の特徴（具体性、苦痛へのすり替えがない、代償を伴う行動）を挙げ、謝罪とは感情表現より約束であり、誠意は何を手放すかで測られる、とまとめています。2番目は最適な時期を述べておらず、3番目は自分の苦痛に話を移すことを避けるという本文に反し、4番目は代償を要件とする本文に反します。
m: 謝罪＝感情の表現ではなく、代償を伴う約束

t: 論旨：代償のない言葉
p: A public apology is easy to criticise. If it comes too early, it seems to be a way of ending the discussion before anyone has understood what happened; if it comes late, it looks forced. Yet the apologies that people accept have a pattern. They name the specific wrong instead of speaking vaguely of 'any offence that may have been caused'. They do not shift attention to the apologiser's own suffering. And they are followed by some action that costs something, since words that cost nothing are easily doubted. These features suggest that an apology is not mainly an expression of feeling. It is a kind of promise, whose sincerity is judged by what the speaker is prepared to give up.
q: 本文の words that cost nothing are easily doubted の含意として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: People believe an apology more when it is backed by something the speaker gives up.
People doubt every apology that is followed by some action.
Apologies should avoid words and consist of silence.
A cheap apology is welcomed because it ends the discussion quickly.
e: 代償のない言葉は疑われやすい、つまり話し手が何かを手放す行動を伴う謝罪のほうが信じられる、という含意です。2番目は逆（行動が続くと疑われる）、3番目の「沈黙」、4番目の「安い謝罪が歓迎される」は本文にありません。
m: 信じられる謝罪＝コストを払う謝罪

t: 文の挿入：週末の誕生
p: For most of history, the idea of a regular day off was unfamiliar. Farmers rested when the weather forced them to, and artisans took holidays tied to religious festivals. [ 1 ] The change came with factory work, which, unlike farming, required people to be at the same place at the same hours every day. Workers who were bound to the clock began to demand a fixed period that belonged to them. [ 2 ] Employers resisted at first, but many discovered that rested workers made fewer mistakes, and the half-holiday gradually became a full two days. [ 3 ] What had begun as a concession to exhausted employees became a market of its own: sport, travel, and entertainment all grew up to fill the time that the working week left over.
q: 次の英文の空所［ 1 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: Rest, in other words, followed the rhythm of nature and belief rather than a calendar of work.
Employers soon realised that workers who never rested were more productive.
Factories therefore closed on the days when the weather was best.
The weekend was invented to keep farmers at work through the winter.
e: 空所の直後に The change came with factory work（変化は工場労働とともに来た）とあるので、その前には「変化する前の状態」が述べられるはずです。「休みは自然や信仰のリズムに従っていた」がそれに当たり、第1・2文の内容のまとめにもなっています。他の選択肢は、工場労働が始まる前の話として成り立ちません。
m: The change の直前には「変化前の状態」が来る

t: 文の挿入：休みの交渉
p: For most of history, the idea of a regular day off was unfamiliar. Farmers rested when the weather forced them to, and artisans took holidays tied to religious festivals. q: 次の英文の空所［ 2 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: Time off, which had once been a matter of custom, thus became a matter of bargaining.
Farmers also began to ask for time off in order to attend the religious festivals of the year.
Workers' demands were therefore granted immediately, and without any argument from employers.
Religious holidays soon disappeared from the calendar altogether in the industrial towns.
e: 前の文で、時計に縛られた労働者が自分たちのための一定の休みを要求し始めた、直後で、雇用者は最初は抵抗した、とあります。したがって「習慣だった休みが交渉の対象になった」が自然です。3番目は直後の resisted と矛盾し、2番目の農民、4番目の宗教的休日の消滅は文脈にありません。
m: 前後の流れ（要求→抵抗）をつなぐ文を選ぶ

q: 次の英文の空所［ 3 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
