Nevertheless, leisure activities remained limited to the wealthy.

t: 文の挿入：辞書は規則集か
p: Many people consult a dictionary as if it were a rulebook, expecting it to say which words are allowed. [ 1 ] The first great dictionaries of English were indeed compiled by men who saw themselves as guardians of the language. Modern lexicographers take a different view. [ 2 ] They collect large bodies of real writing and speech, and a word is included when it is used consistently and widely, whatever the compilers think of it. [ 3 ] This is why a dictionary is revised every few years, and why a word once marked 'slang' may later lose its label without anyone having granted permission.
q: 次の英文の空所［ 1 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: This expectation is understandable, and it has a long history.
Few people, in fact, ever open a dictionary of any kind these days.
Dictionaries have never contained any slang words of any kind, whatever their date.
Lexicographers therefore avoid writing definitions.
e: 直後の文は「最初の大辞典は、言語の番人を自任する人々によって編まれた」で、indeed が前の文を補強しています。辞書を規則集のように使う期待には歴史がある、という内容が合います。2番目は冒頭の Many people と矛盾、3番目は slang を扱う後文と矛盾し、4番目は文脈に根拠がありません。
m: indeed は直前の文を裏づける合図

t: 文の挿入：記録者としての辞書編集者
p: Many people consult a dictionary as if it were a rulebook, expecting it to say which words are allowed. q: 次の英文の空所［ 2 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: Their task, as they understand it, is to record how the language is used, not to decide how it should be used.
Their dictionaries are therefore much shorter than those of earlier times.
They refuse to include any word that is less than a century old.
They are chosen for their skill in persuading people to avoid slang.
e: 空所の前で「現代の編集者は違う見方をする」と述べ、後で「実際の文章や発話を集め、広く一貫して使われる語を載せる」と具体化しています。間に入るのは「使い方を記録するのが仕事で、決めるのが仕事ではない」という説明です。他の選択肢は、後続の具体的な方法につながりません。
m: 抽象的な主張→具体的な方法の間には要約文が入る

In this sense a dictionary is finished once it has been printed.

m: This is why の前には「理由」が置かれる

t: 文の挿入：道路拡張の論理
p: Faced with congestion, the obvious remedy seems to be a wider road. [ 1 ] Yet experience in many cities has shown that new lanes often fill up within a few years, leaving traffic as slow as before. Economists call the effect 'induced demand'. [ 2 ] A faster road makes driving more attractive, so that people who once took the train, or avoided a journey altogether, begin to use the car. [ 3 ] The lesson is not that roads are worthless but that congestion acts as a price that rises until drivers decide the trip is no longer worth making, and building more space merely moves the point at which they decide.
q: 次の英文の空所［ 1 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: The logic is simple: more space should mean less crowding.
This remedy has never been tried in any city.
Most drivers, in fact, prefer narrow roads to wide ones.
Planners therefore agree that wider roads always cause congestion.
e: 直後が Yet experience … has shown that new lanes often fill up（しかし経験では新しい車線はすぐ埋まる）なので、前には「道を広げれば混雑が減るはず」という常識的な理屈が来ます。2番目は「一度も試されていない」で後文の experience と矛盾し、3番目・4番目は逆接 Yet の前提として合いません。
m: Yet の前には「常識的な見方」が来る

t: 文の挿入：大人の楽器学習
p: Adults often assume that musical talent must be discovered in childhood, and that anyone who has not begun young has missed the chance. [ 1 ] Adult learners do have disadvantages: less free time, and a greater fear of sounding foolish. [ 2 ] They can understand why a technique works, and they can practise deliberately rather than merely repeat. [ 3 ] The real obstacle, then, is seldom age itself, but the belief that it is too late.
q: 次の英文の空所［ 1 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: The evidence, however, does not support so gloomy a view.
Children, in fact, learn more slowly than adults in every respect.
Teachers therefore advise adults not to start at all.
Studies show that talent is fixed at birth and cannot be developed.
e: 冒頭は「子どものうちに始めなければ手遅れ」という悲観的な見方で、直後の文は「大人にも不利はある」と認めています。その間に「しかし証拠はそれほど悲観的な見方を支えない」と入れると、逆接の流れが自然です。2番目は「あらゆる点で」と言い過ぎで、3番目・4番目は最後の結論と矛盾します。
m: 悲観的な通説→反論→留保、という流れを追う

t: 文の挿入：「夕焼けは晴れ」
p: Proverbs about the weather are often dismissed as superstition. 'Red sky at night, shepherd's delight' sounds more like a charm than a forecast. [ 1 ] In the middle latitudes, weather systems generally move from west to east. A red sunset means that the sun is shining through dry, dusty air in the west. [ 2 ] A red sky in the morning suggests that the same clear air has already passed, and that moisture may be arriving. [ 3 ]
q: 次の英文の空所［ 1 ］に入れるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
c: Yet there is a reasonable physical explanation behind it.
Meteorologists therefore ignore all traditional sayings.
No one has ever compared such sayings with actual weather.
It is, of course, much older than any form of agriculture.
e: 前は「呪文のように聞こえる」という否定的な評価、直後は「中緯度では天気は西から東へ移動する」という科学的説明です。その間に逆接の Yet で「それでも合理的な物理的説明がある」と入れると、流れが通ります。他の選択肢は、直後の科学的説明を導きません。
m: 否定的評価→Yet→科学的な説明の流れ

t: 文の挿入：夕焼けの次の日

t: 空所補充：小説と共感
p: Reading fiction is sometimes said to make people more ( 1 ), since it invites them to follow the thoughts of characters unlike themselves. The evidence for this claim is, however, ( 2 ). Some experiments find a small effect, while others find none, and it is hard to separate the effect of reading from the fact that people who already care about others may simply choose to read more. What can be said with more confidence is that fiction offers practice in ( 3 ) another point of view, even if it does not ( 4 ) anyone's character.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 1 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: sympathetic to others
dependent on other people
suspicious of strangers
superior to others
e: 小説は自分と異なる登場人物の考えをたどらせるので、「他者に共感的になる」と言われる、という文脈です。dependent（頼る）、suspicious（疑い深い）、superior（優越した）は、他人の考えをたどることから生まれる性質として不自然です。
m: follow the thoughts of others → 共感

t: 空所補充：証拠は一定しない

m: Some … while others … → 結果はまちまち（mixed）

t: 空所補充：別の視点を想像する
p: Reading fiction is sometimes said to make people more ( 1 ), since it invites them to follow the thoughts of characters unlike themselves. The evidence for this claim is, however, ( 2 ). Some experiments find a small effect, while others find none, and it is hard to separate the effect of reading from the fact that people who already care about others may simply choose to read more. What can be said with more confidence is that fiction offers practice in ( 3 ) another point of view, even if it does not ( 4 ) anyone's character.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 3 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: imagining
abandoning
avoiding
ignoring
e: 筆者が確信を持って言えるのは、小説が別の視点を「想像する」練習になることです。「捨てる」「避ける」「無視する」は、他者の考えをたどるという冒頭の説明と合いません。practice in ＋動名詞の形にも注意します。
m: practice in doing＝〜する練習

t: 空所補充：性格を変える
p: Reading fiction is sometimes said to make people more ( 1 ), since it invites them to follow the thoughts of characters unlike themselves. The evidence for this claim is, however, ( 2 ). Some experiments find a small effect, while others find none, and it is hard to separate the effect of reading from the fact that people who already care about others may simply choose to read more. What can be said with more confidence is that fiction offers practice in ( 3 ) another point of view, even if it does not ( 4 ) anyone's character.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 4 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: transform
transfer
translate
transmit
e: even if it does not ( 4 ) anyone's character は「誰かの性格を変える」の意味で、transform（根本的に変える）が合います。transfer、translate、transmit は character を目的語にとって意味をなしません。
m: transform＝すっかり変える

t: 空所補充：子どもの夏の長さ
p: Many adults remember the summers of childhood as ( 1 ), and the years of later life as passing too quickly. One explanation is that novelty slows our sense of time: a child meets new things every day, and each new experience leaves a distinct memory, whereas a routine adult year leaves very few. Looking back, we judge a period by the number of memories it contains, so that a year of ( 2 ) seems shorter than a week of discovery. If this is right, the remedy for the speed of life is to ( 3 ) our days with experiences worth remembering.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 1 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: seemingly endless
carelessly forgotten
strangely silent
surprisingly brief
e: 後半の「後年は速く過ぎる」と対比されるので、子どもの夏は「果てしなく長く感じられる」ものです。forgotten（忘れられた）や silent（静かな）は対比になりません。surprisingly brief（意外に短い）は、後年が速く過ぎるという対比と逆向きになります。
m: too quickly と対になる語＝endless

t: 空所補充：変化のない一年
p: Many adults remember the summers of childhood as ( 1 ), and the years of later life as passing too quickly. One explanation is that novelty slows our sense of time: a child meets new things every day, and each new experience leaves a distinct memory, whereas a routine adult year leaves very few. Looking back, we judge a period by the number of memories it contains, so that a year of ( 2 ) seems shorter than a week of discovery. If this is right, the remedy for the speed of life is to ( 3 ) our days with experiences worth remembering.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 2 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: routine
discovery
surprise
adventure
e: 前の文で「決まりきった大人の一年は記憶がごくわずか」と述べているので、a week of discovery と対比される a year of routine が入ります。discovery、adventure、surprise は、いずれも記憶を増やす側にあたり、「短く感じられる一年」に合いません。
m: a week of discovery と対比される語を探す

t: 空所補充：日々を満たす
p: Many adults remember the summers of childhood as ( 1 ), and the years of later life as passing too quickly. One explanation is that novelty slows our sense of time: a child meets new things every day, and each new experience leaves a distinct memory, whereas a routine adult year leaves very few. Looking back, we judge a period by the number of memories it contains, so that a year of ( 2 ) seems shorter than a week of discovery. If this is right, the remedy for the speed of life is to ( 3 ) our days with experiences worth remembering.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 3 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: fill
empty
shorten
forget
e: 記憶の数で時間を判断するという説明から、解決策は日々を記憶に残る経験で「満たす」ことです。empty（空にする）、shorten（短くする）、forget（忘れる）では、with experiences worth remembering とつながりません。fill A with B の形です。
m: fill A with B＝AをBで満たす

t: 空所補充：森林火災の見方
p: Forest fires are usually seen as ( 1 ), but ecologists note that many forests depend on fire. Some pine cones open only in intense heat, and the cleared ground gives their seedlings the light they need. A policy of putting out every fire at once therefore has an unexpected cost. It allows dead wood to ( 2 ) year after year, so that when a fire does come, it burns with a force ( 3 ) anything a natural fire would have produced.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 1 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: pure disasters
valuable gifts
harmless events
regular festivals
e: but 以下で「多くの森林は火に依存する」と対比されるので、通常は「純粋な災害」と見られているという流れです。valuable gifts（貴重な贈り物）や harmless events（害のない出来事）は、but 以下の意外な指摘と対比になりません。
m: but の前後は対比。通常の見方を探す

t: 空所補充：枯れ木が増える
p: Forest fires are usually seen as ( 1 ), but ecologists note that many forests depend on fire. Some pine cones open only in intense heat, and the cleared ground gives their seedlings the light they need. A policy of putting out every fire at once therefore has an unexpected cost. It allows dead wood to ( 2 ) year after year, so that when a fire does come, it burns with a force ( 3 ) anything a natural fire would have produced.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 2 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: accumulate
evaporate slowly
dissolve
disappear completely
e: 火災をすべて消すと、枯れ木が年々「たまる」ので、後で起きる火災が激しくなります。evaporate（蒸発する）、dissolve（溶ける）、disappear（消える）では、後の「より強い力で燃える」につながりません。
m: year after year と結びつく動詞は accumulate

t: 空所補充：自然の火災との比較
p: Forest fires are usually seen as ( 1 ), but ecologists note that many forests depend on fire. Some pine cones open only in intense heat, and the cleared ground gives their seedlings the light they need. A policy of putting out every fire at once therefore has an unexpected cost. It allows dead wood to ( 2 ) year after year, so that when a fire does come, it burns with a force ( 3 ) anything a natural fire would have produced.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 3 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: far greater than
no different from
much weaker than
scarcely greater than
e: 枯れ木がたまった状態で起きる火災は、自然の火災より「はるかに激しい」はずです。「違いがない」「ずっと弱い」「ほとんど大きくない」では、消火政策の予想外の代償という文脈に合いません。
m: unexpected cost → より激しい火災

t: 空所補充：診断の素早さ
p: Doctors are trained to reach a diagnosis quickly, since in an emergency hesitation can ( 1 ) lives. But the habit has a cost. Once a doctor has settled on an explanation, later information tends to be read in its light, and facts that do not fit are explained away instead of being ( 2 ). Hospitals that encourage a second opinion, or that ask staff to name one alternative before deciding, report fewer errors. The aim is not to make doctors ( 3 ) but to keep the first idea from closing the question too soon.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 1 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: cost
save
improve
prolong
e: 救急では迷っていると命を落とす、というのが素早い診断を訓練する理由です。hesitation can cost lives（ためらいは命を失わせることがある）が文脈に合います。save（救う）は、ためらいが命を救うことになり、理由として成り立ちません。improve、prolong も同様です。
m: hesitation can cost lives＝ためらいが命取りに

t: 空所補充：合わない事実の扱い
p: Doctors are trained to reach a diagnosis quickly, since in an emergency hesitation can ( 1 ) lives. But the habit has a cost. Once a doctor has settled on an explanation, later information tends to be read in its light, and facts that do not fit are explained away instead of being ( 2 ). Hospitals that encourage a second opinion, or that ask staff to name one alternative before deciding, report fewer errors. The aim is not to make doctors ( 3 ) but to keep the first idea from closing the question too soon.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 2 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: taken seriously
kept secret from others
repeated aloud again
paid for
e: 最初の説明に合わない事実を「説明して片づけて」しまい、本来なら「真剣に受け止める」べきだ、という文脈です。explained away instead of being taken seriously が自然です。kept secret、repeated aloud、paid for は、診断の過程で事実を扱う表現として不適切です。
m: explain away（言いくるめて片づける）の反対を考える

t: 空所補充：医師を迷わせたいのではない
p: Doctors are trained to reach a diagnosis quickly, since in an emergency hesitation can ( 1 ) lives. But the habit has a cost. Once a doctor has settled on an explanation, later information tends to be read in its light, and facts that do not fit are explained away instead of being ( 2 ). Hospitals that encourage a second opinion, or that ask staff to name one alternative before deciding, report fewer errors. The aim is not to make doctors ( 3 ) but to keep the first idea from closing the question too soon.
q: 次の英文の空所（ 3 ）に入れるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
c: indecisive
experienced
honest
tired
e: 素早い診断の訓練を前提に、狙いは医師を「優柔不断にする」ことではなく、最初の考えに結論を閉ざさせないことだ、という流れです。experienced、honest、tired は、not … but … の対比として、直前の文脈と結びつきません。
m: not A but B の A には「誤解されがちな点」が入る

t: 語句の意味：beside the point
p: Speed-reading courses promise to double the pace at which we read, but for many kinds of text speed is (1)【beside the point】. A poem, a legal argument or a difficult proof is not a package of information to be (2)【got through】 as quickly as possible; it is a structure that must be rebuilt in the reader's mind, and the rebuilding takes the time it takes. Skimming has its uses, of course, but it is an error to (3)【mistake it for】 reading itself.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: not relevant to what really matters
the main attraction of such courses
hard to measure precisely
less important than it used to be
e: beside the point は「的外れで、要点と関係がない」という成句です。ここでは、詩や論証のような文章では読む速さは本質と関係がない、という意味になります。「主な魅力」は promise to double the pace と文脈が逆、「測りにくい」「以前ほど重要でない」は成句の意味と異なります。
m: beside the point＝的外れ、無関係

t: 語句の意味：get through
p: Speed-reading courses promise to double the pace at which we read, but for many kinds of text speed is (1)【beside the point】. A poem, a legal argument or a difficult proof is not a package of information to be (2)【got through】 as quickly as possible; it is a structure that must be rebuilt in the reader's mind, and the rebuilding takes the time it takes. Skimming has its uses, of course, but it is an error to (3)【mistake it for】 reading itself.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: completed in a hurry
understood in great depth
examined with care
taken apart and studied
e: get through は「（仕事・文章などを）なんとか済ませる、やり終える」という意味です。ここでは情報の包みとして急いで読み終えるもの、ということです。直後の as quickly as possible とも合います。understood in depth や examined with care は、続く「頭の中で作り直す構造」の側の説明になっています。
m: get through＝やり終える。as quickly as possible に注目

t: 語句の意味：mistake A for B
p: Speed-reading courses promise to double the pace at which we read, but for many kinds of text speed is (1)【beside the point】. A poem, a legal argument or a difficult proof is not a package of information to be (2)【got through】 as quickly as possible; it is a structure that must be rebuilt in the reader's mind, and the rebuilding takes the time it takes. Skimming has its uses, of course, but it is an error to (3)【mistake it for】 reading itself.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: confuse it with
prefer it to
compare it with
protect it from
e: mistake A for B は「AをBと取り違える」です。ここでは skimming（飛ばし読み）を reading そのものと取り違えるのは誤りだ、という意味になります。prefer A to B（AをBより好む）、compare A with B、protect A from B では、mistake の用法と合いません。
m: mistake A for B＝AをBと取り違える

t: 語句の意味：seen better days
p: The bakery on the corner of our street had (1)【seen better days】 by the time my family arrived, but nobody in the neighbourhood could imagine (2)【doing without it】. The owner, a retired sailor with a loud laugh, (3)【made a point of】 learning the name of every child who came in for bread, and he never let a stranger leave without a remark about the weather.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: was no longer in good condition
had recently been repaired by its owner
was busier than it had ever been before
was admired by the many tourists who visited
e: see better days は「落ちぶれた、昔のほうが良かった」という成句です。直後の but nobody could imagine doing without it（それでも誰もそれなしの生活は想像できなかった）という逆接とも合います。「修理された」「かつてなく忙しい」「観光客に称賛された」は成句の意味ではありません。
m: have seen better days＝すっかり古びた

t: 語句の意味：do without
p: The bakery on the corner of our street had (1)【seen better days】 by the time my family arrived, but nobody in the neighbourhood could imagine (2)【doing without it】. The owner, a retired sailor with a loud laugh, (3)【made a point of】 learning the name of every child who came in for bread, and he never let a stranger leave without a remark about the weather.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: managing in its absence
making good use of it
being angry with it all day
paying a high price for it
e: do without は「〜なしで済ます」です。doing without it は「それなしでやっていくこと」で、近所の人はパン屋がなくなった生活を想像できなかった、という意味です。make use of、be angry about、pay for は、この成句の意味ではありません。
m: do without A＝Aなしで済ます

t: 語句の意味：make a point of
p: The bakery on the corner of our street had (1)【seen better days】 by the time my family arrived, but nobody in the neighbourhood could imagine (2)【doing without it】. The owner, a retired sailor with a loud laugh, (3)【made a point of】 learning the name of every child who came in for bread, and he never let a stranger leave without a remark about the weather.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: made an effort to do it
often forgot all about doing it
refused on principle to bother
was too busy to bother with it
e: make a point of doing は「わざわざ〜するようにしている」という成句です。made a point of learning the name of every child は、子ども全員の名前を意識して覚えるようにしていた、という意味になります。forgot、refused、was too busy は、すべて「覚えていた」という文脈に反します。
m: make a point of doing＝努めて〜する

t: 語句の意味：hold sway
p: Public opinion is often said to (1)【hold sway】 over politicians, yet leaders, (2)【by and large】, pay attention only to the opinions of those likely to vote. A policy that (3)【runs counter to】 the wishes of the majority may therefore survive for years if the majority is not paying attention.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: have great influence
remain unchanged
be easily ignored
be carefully measured
e: hold sway over は「〜を支配する、大きな影響力をもつ」です。「世論は政治家に影響力をもつと言われるが、実際は…」という逆接の流れに合います。「変わらない」「簡単に無視される」「慎重に測られる」はいずれも成句の意味ではありません。
m: hold sway over A＝Aを支配する

t: 語句の意味：by and large
p: Public opinion is often said to (1)【hold sway】 over politicians, yet leaders, (2)【by and large】, pay attention only to the opinions of those likely to vote. A policy that (3)【runs counter to】 the wishes of the majority may therefore survive for years if the majority is not paying attention.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: on the whole
without exception
from time to time
in a rather hurried way
e: by and large は「概して、全般的に」です。on the whole が最も近い言い換えです。without exception（例外なく）は「概して」と強さが違い、from time to time は頻度、in a hurried way は様子の話で、いずれも異なります。
m: by and large＝on the whole＝概して

t: 語句の意味：run counter to
p: Public opinion is often said to (1)【hold sway】 over politicians, yet leaders, (2)【by and large】, pay attention only to the opinions of those likely to vote. A policy that (3)【runs counter to】 the wishes of the majority may therefore survive for years if the majority is not paying attention.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: goes against
is combined with
runs faster than
is supported by
e: run counter to は「〜に反する」です。a policy that runs counter to the wishes of the majority は「多数派の意向に反する政策」で、それでも多数派が注目していなければ長く続く、という内容です。support や combine は逆の方向、run faster than は文字通りの誤読です。
m: counter＝逆。run counter to＝逆行する

t: 語句の意味：do wonders for
p: People who swim in cold water all year often say it (1)【does wonders for】 their mood, and some doctors believe them. Yet the evidence is thin, and enthusiasts tend to (2)【play down】 the risks, which are real for anyone with a weak heart. It would be unwise to (3)【write off】 the claims entirely, but equally unwise to (4)【take them at face value】.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: has a very good effect on
makes little difference to
is the cause of damage to
is paid for by
e: do wonders for は「〜に絶大な効果がある」という成句です。ここでは気分を大いに良くする、という意味です。makes little difference は逆の意味、damage の原因や is paid for by は文脈に合いません。some doctors believe them とも整合します。
m: do wonders for A＝Aにすばらしい効果がある

t: 語句の意味：play down
p: People who swim in cold water all year often say it (1)【does wonders for】 their mood, and some doctors believe them. Yet the evidence is thin, and enthusiasts tend to (2)【play down】 the risks, which are real for anyone with a weak heart. It would be unwise to (3)【write off】 the claims entirely, but equally unwise to (4)【take them at face value】.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: treat them as less important
exaggerate them to others
list them in public
measure them with great care
e: play down は「〜を軽く扱う、重要でないように見せる」です。熱心な愛好者がリスクを軽く見せる、という意味です。exaggerate はまさに逆で、list や measure は成句の意味ではありません。直前の Yet the evidence is thin から、慎重な筆者の視点がわかります。
m: play down↔play up（強調する）

t: 語句の意味：write off
p: People who swim in cold water all year often say it (1)【does wonders for】 their mood, and some doctors believe them. Yet the evidence is thin, and enthusiasts tend to (2)【play down】 the risks, which are real for anyone with a weak heart. It would be unwise to (3)【write off】 the claims entirely, but equally unwise to (4)【take them at face value】.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: dismiss them as worthless
record them in writing
pay them back in full
rewrite them for greater clarity
e: write off は「〜を無価値なものとして切り捨てる、見限る」です。直後の equally unwise to … take them at face value と合わせて、「主張を全面的に退けるのも、鵜呑みにするのも賢明でない」という筆者の中立的な立場になります。他の選択肢は write の字面にひかれた誤りです。
m: write off＝見切りをつける、帳消しにする

t: 語句の意味：take at face value
p: People who swim in cold water all year often say it (1)【does wonders for】 their mood, and some doctors believe them. Yet the evidence is thin, and enthusiasts tend to (2)【play down】 the risks, which are real for anyone with a weak heart. It would be unwise to (3)【write off】 the claims entirely, but equally unwise to (4)【take them at face value】.
q: 【 】で示した下線部（4）の意味・内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: accept them as they appear
judge them mainly by who said them
reject them as soon as they are heard
repeat them again to other people
e: take A at face value は「Aを額面どおりに受け取る」で、疑わずにそのまま信じるという意味です。前半の dismiss と対になって、どちらの極端も避けるべきだと述べています。judge by who said them や reject は意味が異なり、repeat は成句と無関係です。
m: face value＝額面。そのまま受け取る

t: 下線部和訳：初期の測量士
p: (1)【Had the early surveyors not been willing to walk every ridge and valley, our maps would still be little more than guesses.】 The work was slow, and it was dangerous: (2)【it was not until the instruments were carried up the mountain by many men that the height could be measured with any confidence.】 Yet (3)【the surveyors cared no more about fame than the mountains cared about the surveyors.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 初期の測量士たちがすべての尾根や谷を労をいとわず歩いていなかったら、私たちの地図は今でも推測の域をほとんど出ていないだろう。
初期の測量士たちはすべての尾根や谷を歩こうとはしなかったが、それでも私たちの地図は今では推測以上のものになっているのである。
初期の測量士たちはすべての尾根や谷を歩く意志があったので、私たちの地図はやがて推測以上のものになっていくだろうと言われている。
初期の測量士たちがすべての尾根や谷を歩く労をいとわなかったので、私たちの地図は今でも推測にすぎないものにとどまってしまっている。
e: Had S not been … は if S had not been … の倒置で、過去の事実に反する仮定です。主節の would still be … は「今でもまだ…だろう」という帰結で、「歩いてくれたから地図が推測を超えた」ことを逆から述べています。2番目は仮定を打ち消し、3番目は未来の話にし、4番目は仮定法を事実の因果に取り違えています。
m: Had S p.p.＝If S had p.p. の倒置。事実と反対

t: 下線部和訳：山の高さの測定
p: (1)【Had the early surveyors not been willing to walk every ridge and valley, our maps would still be little more than guesses.】 The work was slow, and it was dangerous: (2)【it was not until the instruments were carried up the mountain by many men that the height could be measured with any confidence.】 Yet (3)【the surveyors cared no more about fame than the mountains cared about the surveyors.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 器具が大勢の人の手で山の上へ運び上げられて初めて、高さをある程度の確信をもって測ることができた。
器具が山の上へ運び上げられるまでに、大勢の人がある程度の確信をもって高さを測ることができた。
器具が大勢の人の手で山の上へ運び上げられても、高さをある程度の確信をもって測ることはできなかった。
大勢の人が器具を山の上へ運ぶまでもなく、高さをある程度の確信をもって測れるようになった。
e: It was not until A that B は「Aして初めてBした」です。器具が山に運び上げられて初めて、高さが確信をもって測れるようになった、という意味です。2番目は until を「までに」と取り違え、3番目は否定の位置を誤り、4番目は not until を「〜するまでもなく」と誤訳しています。
m: It was not until A that B＝Aして初めてB

t: 下線部和訳：名声を気にしない
p: (1)【Had the early surveyors not been willing to walk every ridge and valley, our maps would still be little more than guesses.】 The work was slow, and it was dangerous: (2)【it was not until the instruments were carried up the mountain by many men that the height could be measured with any confidence.】 Yet (3)【the surveyors cared no more about fame than the mountains cared about the surveyors.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 山々が測量士たちを気にかけないのと同じように、測量士たちも名声を気にかけなかった。
測量士たちは名声を気にかけていたが、山々が測量士たちを気にかけた以上のものではなかったのである。
山々が測量士たちを気にかけた以上に、測量士たちは名声を気にかけていた。
測量士たちは名声を気にかけなかったが、山々のほうは測量士たちのことをいつも気にかけていた。
e: A no more … than B は「Bが…でないのと同様にAも…でない」という、両方を否定する構文（クジラの公式）です。測量士が名声を気にしないのは、山が測量士を気にしないのと同じ、という意味です。他の選択肢は、どちらかを肯定していたり、比較の向きを逆にしていたりします。
m: A no more … than B＝BでないようにAでもない

t: 下線部和訳：電話と正直さ
p: A letter forces its writer to decide what to say before saying it. (1)【A telephone call, on the other hand, allows one to think aloud, and it is hardly surprising that many people find it easier to be honest on the phone.】 Yet (2)【the very ease that makes conversation pleasant is what makes it unreliable as a record: no one can be held to words that have vanished into the air.】 For this reason, (3)【important agreements are, even today, the last things people are willing to settle by voice alone.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 一方、電話では考えながら声に出して話せるので、電話のほうが正直になりやすいと感じる人が多いのも、ほとんど驚くに当たらない。
一方、電話では考えを声に出して話すことが許されないので、電話では正直になりにくいと感じる人が多いのは、まったく驚くべきことである。
一方、電話のほうが手紙より正直であると考える人は、まず考えを声に出して整理する必要があるため、驚くほど少ない。
一方、電話では声に出して考えることができるが、電話のほうが正直になりやすいと感じる人が多いのは、大いに驚くべきことである。
e: hardly surprising は「ほとんど驚くに当たらない」で、think aloud は「考えを声に出して話す」です。電話は考えながら話せるので正直になりやすい、という自然な理由づけです。2番目は allows を逆にし、3番目は主語と内容が変わり、4番目は hardly を誤って「大いに」と訳しています。
m: hardly surprising＝驚くに当たらない

t: 下線部和訳：会話の気軽さ
p: A letter forces its writer to decide what to say before saying it. (1)【A telephone call, on the other hand, allows one to think aloud, and it is hardly surprising that many people find it easier to be honest on the phone.】 Yet (2)【the very ease that makes conversation pleasant is what makes it unreliable as a record: no one can be held to words that have vanished into the air.】 For this reason, (3)【important agreements are, even today, the last things people are willing to settle by voice alone.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 会話を心地よくするまさにその気軽さが、会話を記録として頼りないものにする。空中に消えた言葉の責任は誰にも問えない。
会話が記録として頼りないものであることが、会話を心地よくする気軽さを生んでおり、空中に消えた言葉を責められる人はいない。
会話を心地よくする気軽さがあれば、会話は記録として頼れるものになり、空中に消えた言葉には責任を問える人がいる。
会話の記録は気軽さを心地よくするためにあり、空中に消えた言葉は結局のところ誰にも責任を問うことができない。
e: the very ease that makes conversation pleasant（会話を心地よくするまさにその気軽さ）が、what makes it unreliable as a record（会話を記録として頼りなくするもの）だ、という構造です。2番目は因果を逆にし、3番目は否定を落とし、4番目は文構造を取り違えています。コロン以下は理由の説明です。
m: the very A＝まさにそのA。S is what ～＝Sが～の原因

t: 下線部和訳：重要な合意
p: A letter forces its writer to decide what to say before saying it. (1)【A telephone call, on the other hand, allows one to think aloud, and it is hardly surprising that many people find it easier to be honest on the phone.】 Yet (2)【the very ease that makes conversation pleasant is what makes it unreliable as a record: no one can be held to words that have vanished into the air.】 For this reason, (3)【important agreements are, even today, the last things people are willing to settle by voice alone.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 重要な合意こそ、今日でさえ、人々が口頭だけで決めることを最もしたがらない事柄である。
重要な合意は、今日でも、人々がほかの事柄をすべて口頭で決め終えた後に、最後に口頭だけで決める事柄である。
重要な合意は、今日では、人々が口頭だけで決めたがる最初の事柄である。
重要な合意を口頭だけで決めようとする人は、今日では最後の世代になりつつあり、その数は年々減っている。
e: the last things people are willing to settle by voice alone は、「人々が口頭だけで決めようとする最後の（＝もっとも決めようとしない）事柄」で、重要な合意は口頭だけでは決めたがらない、という意味です。2番目は last を「順番の最後」の意味にしてしまい、3番目は逆で、4番目は last を「最後の世代」に取り違えています。
m: the last A to do＝もっとも〜しそうにないA

t: 下線部和訳：農家の帳面
p: Farmers in dry regions keep records that outsiders rarely see. (1)【Had it not been for the notebooks passed from parent to child, the pattern of the last three droughts would long ago have been forgotten.】 These books hold (2)【not rainfall figures so much as small observations of when the swallows arrived and which wells failed first.】 Their authors would be surprised to learn that (3)【climate scientists now treat such scraps as evidence no less valuable than the readings of an official station.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 親から子へ受け継がれてきた帳面がなかったなら、直近三度の干ばつの経過は、とうの昔に忘れ去られていただろう。
親から子へ受け継がれてきた帳面がなかったので、直近三度の干ばつの経過は、とうの昔に完全に忘れ去られてしまった。
親から子へ受け継がれてきた帳面があるおかげで、直近三度の干ばつの経過は、決して忘れ去られないだろう。
親から子へ受け継がれてきた帳面がなかったとしても、直近三度の干ばつの経過は、決して忘れ去られなかっただろう。
e: Had it not been for A, S would have p.p. は「もしAがなかったなら、Sはとっくに…されていただろう」という、倒置による仮定法過去完了です（if it had not been for の倒置）。2番目は事実の過去形に、3番目は肯定の事実に、4番目は仮定部分の意味を逆にしています。
m: Had it not been for A＝もしAがなかったなら

t: 下線部和訳：雨量よりも観察
p: Farmers in dry regions keep records that outsiders rarely see. q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 雨量の数字というよりも、むしろツバメがいつ来たか、どの井戸が最初に枯れたかといった小さな観察
雨量の数字だけでなく、ツバメがいつ来たか、どの井戸が最初に枯れたかといった小さな観察を、あわせて書き留めたもの
ツバメがいつ来たかよりも、雨量の数字や最初に枯れた井戸を詳しく記録している、几帳面な観察

m: not A so much as B＝AというよりむしろB

t: 下線部和訳：断片の価値
p: Farmers in dry regions keep records that outsiders rarely see. (1)【Had it not been for the notebooks passed from parent to child, the pattern of the last three droughts would long ago have been forgotten.】 These books hold (2)【not rainfall figures so much as small observations of when the swallows arrived and which wells failed first.】 Their authors would be surprised to learn that (3)【climate scientists now treat such scraps as evidence no less valuable than the readings of an official station.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 気候学者たちは今では、そうした断片を、公式観測所の測定値に劣らず価値のある証拠として扱っている。
気候学者たちは今では、そうした断片を、公式観測所の測定値よりもはるかに価値のある証拠として扱っている。
気候学者たちは今では、そうした断片を、公式観測所の測定値ほどには価値のない証拠として扱っている。
気候学者たちは今では、そうした断片を、公式観測所の測定値の代わりになる証拠として扱っている。

t: 下線部和訳：背景音に慣れた私たち
p: Attitudes to silence differ. (1)【So accustomed are we to background sound that a room without any seems to many people not peaceful but faintly threatening.】 Architects who design concert halls know the problem well: (2)【with the audience seated and the doors closed, the quiet must be complete enough that a whisper reaches the back row, yet not so complete that listeners become aware of their own breathing.】 (3)【Whether silence is welcomed or feared depends less on the quiet itself than on what the listener expects to hear in it.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 私たちは背景の音にあまりに慣れているので、音がまったくない部屋は、多くの人には穏やかではなく、かすかに不気味に感じられる。
私たちは背景の音にあまりに慣れているが、音がまったくない部屋は、多くの人にとって穏やかであり、同時にかすかに不気味でもあるのだ。
背景の音に慣れていない人は、音がまったくない部屋を穏やかだと感じるのではなく、むしろかすかに不気味だと感じるものである。
背景の音に慣れるほど、音がまったくない部屋は多くの人にとって穏やかになり、不気味に感じられることもまったくなくなる。
e: So accustomed are we to A that … は So … that の倒置で、「私たちはAにとても慣れているので…」の意味です。not peaceful but faintly threatening は「穏やかではなく、かすかに脅威を感じさせる」（not A but B）です。2番目は so … that の因果を逆接にし、3番目は主語を変え、4番目は結果を逆にしています。
m: So ～ that の倒置。結果は that 節

t: 下線部和訳：コンサートホールの静けさ
p: Attitudes to silence differ. q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 聴衆が着席し扉が閉まった状態で、静けさは、ささやきが後列に届くほど完全でなければならないが、聴き手が自分の呼吸に気づくほど完全であってもならない。
聴衆が着席して扉を閉めたとき、静けさは、後列にささやきが届かない程度で、聴き手が自分の呼吸に気づくほど完全でなければならない。
聴衆が着席し扉が閉まっていれば、静けさは、ささやきが後列に届くほど完全でなくてもよいが、聴き手が自分の呼吸に気づかないほど完全でなければならない。
聴衆が着席し扉が閉まった状態で、ささやきが後列に届くほど静けさが完全であれば、聴き手は自分の呼吸に気づくほど静けさを意識する。
e: with the audience seated and the doors closed は付帯状況（「聴衆が着席し扉が閉まった状態で」）です。enough that … は「…するほど十分に」、not so … that は「…するほど〜ではない」で、静けさに下限と上限があることを示します。他の選択肢は、下限と上限の関係を取り違えています。
m: with O C（付帯状況）、enough that／not so that の対比

t: 下線部和訳：静けさを歓迎するか
p: Attitudes to silence differ. (1)【So accustomed are we to background sound that a room without any seems to many people not peaceful but faintly threatening.】 Architects who design concert halls know the problem well: (2)【with the audience seated and the doors closed, the quiet must be complete enough that a whisper reaches the back row, yet not so complete that listeners become aware of their own breathing.】 (3)【Whether silence is welcomed or feared depends less on the quiet itself than on what the listener expects to hear in it.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 静けさが歓迎されるか恐れられるかは、静けさそのものよりも、聞き手がその中で何を聞くと予期しているかに左右される。
静けさが歓迎されるか恐れられるかは、聞き手が予期することよりも、静けさそのものによりいっそう多く左右されるものである。
静けさが歓迎されるか恐れられるかに、聞き手が何を予期するかは、静けさそのもの以上に影響を与えない。
静けさが歓迎されることも恐れられることもないなら、聞き手が静けさの中で何を聞くと予期するかには、一切左右されない。

m: depend less on A than on B＝AよりBに左右される

t: 下線部和訳：数字は決定の産物
p: Statistics have a reputation for honesty that they do not entirely deserve. (1)【It is a rare figure that is not the product of a decision about what to count and what to leave out.】 (2)【A government that reports the number of the unemployed can hardly avoid defining who is looking for work, and every definition excludes someone.】 This does not mean that numbers are lies; (3)【it means that they should never be quoted without some account of how they were made.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（1）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 何を数え何を除くかという決定の産物ではない数字は、まれである。
何を数え何を除くかを決めて作られた数字は、まれにしか存在しない。
何を数え何を除くかという決定が行われる数字は、ほとんどない。
まれな数字だけが、何を数えるかという決定の産物であり、除外は行わない。
e: It is a rare figure that is not … は「…でないような数字はまれだ」という否定を重ねた言い方で、実質的には「ほとんどの数字は決定の産物だ」という意味です。2番目は否定を落とし、3番目は決定が行われることを少数派にしており、4番目は rare の対象をすり替えています。
m: rare ～ that is not …＝…でない～はまれ（＝大半は…）

t: 下線部和訳：失業者の定義
p: Statistics have a reputation for honesty that they do not entirely deserve. (1)【It is a rare figure that is not the product of a decision about what to count and what to leave out.】 (2)【A government that reports the number of the unemployed can hardly avoid defining who is looking for work, and every definition excludes someone.】 This does not mean that numbers are lies; (3)【it means that they should never be quoted without some account of how they were made.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（2）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: 失業者の数を報告する政府は、誰が職を探しているのかを定義することをほとんど避けられず、どの定義も誰かを除外する。

失業者の数を報告する政府が定義することを避けるなら、職を探している人はほとんど除外されない。
e: can hardly avoid doing は「〜することをほとんど避けられない」で、hardly が can を否定しています。every definition excludes someone は「どんな定義も誰かを除外する」です。2番目は文の意味を変え、3番目は hardly を define にかけ、4番目は仮定法的に誤読しています。
m: can hardly do＝ほとんど〜できない

t: 下線部和訳：数字の引用
p: Statistics have a reputation for honesty that they do not entirely deserve. (1)【It is a rare figure that is not the product of a decision about what to count and what to leave out.】 (2)【A government that reports the number of the unemployed can hardly avoid defining who is looking for work, and every definition excludes someone.】 This does not mean that numbers are lies; (3)【it means that they should never be quoted without some account of how they were made.】
q: 【 】で示した下線部（3）の和訳として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: それは、数字は、どのように作られたかの説明を添えずには決して引用されるべきではないということを意味する。
それは、数字は、どのように作られたかの説明を添えた場合にのみ、決して引用されるべきではないということを意味する。
それは、数字は、どのように作られたかの説明がなくても、引用されるべきだということを意味する。
それは、数字を決して引用してはならず、作り方の説明だけを引用すべきだということを意味する。
e: never … without ～ は二重否定の形で、「～なしには決して…ない」つまり「…するときは必ず～を添える」という意味です。2番目は否定のかかる範囲を誤り、3番目は without を無視して逆の意味にし、4番目は never を引用そのものの禁止にしています。
m: never A without B＝AするときはいつもBを伴う

t: 誤り指摘：suggest that 節の動詞
p: (a)［The consultant suggested］ (b)［that the firm reduce］ (c)［its spending on advertising and that］ (d)［the managers revises］ (e)［the budget every quarter.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (d) the managers revises
(a) The consultant suggested
(b) that the firm reduce
(c) its spending on advertising and that
(e) the budget every quarter.
e: suggest, recommend, insist などの後の that 節では、動詞は原形（仮定法現在。イギリス英語では should＋原形）を使います。the managers revises は三人称単数の -s が付いているうえ、複数主語にも合わないので、revise が正しい形です。(b)の reduce は同じ規則に従って正しい形で、(a)(c)(e)に誤りはありません。
m: suggest that S＋動詞の原形

t: 誤り指摘：be used to＋動名詞
p: Since moving to the city, Ken (a)［has become used］ (b)［to getting up］ (c)［early, but he still］ (d)［isn't used］ (e)［to eat alone in the evenings.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (e) to eat alone in the evenings.
(a) has become used
(b) to getting up
(c) early, but he still
(d) isn't used
e: be used to は「〜に慣れている」で、to は前置詞なので後ろは名詞か動名詞です。したがって(e)は to eating alone in the evenings が正しい形です。(a)の become used to と(b)の getting up は正しい形です。used to do（かつて〜したものだ）の不定詞の to と混同しないことが大切です。
m: be used to doing（慣れている）

t: 誤り指摘：despite と in spite of
p: (a)［Despite of］ (b)［the heavy rain,］ (c)［the match was held as planned,］ (d)［to the delight of］ (e)［the spectators.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (a) Despite of
(b) the heavy rain,
(c) the match was held as planned,
(d) to the delight of
(e) the spectators.
e: despite は前置詞そのもので「〜にもかかわらず」の意味です。of を付けて despite of とするのは誤りで、Despite the heavy rain か In spite of the heavy rain と言います（in spite of の形と混同した誤り）。(d)の to the delight of は「〜が喜んだことに」という正しい成句です。
m: despite（of なし）＝in spite of

t: 誤り指摘：such a と so の使い分け
p: (a)［It was］ (b)［so a pleasant evening］ (c)［that we decided］ (d)［to walk home］ (e)［instead of taking a taxi.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (b) so a pleasant evening
(a) It was
(c) that we decided
(d) to walk home
(e) instead of taking a taxi.
e: 「とても〜な…」の名詞句では、such a＋形容詞＋名詞の語順を使います。so を使うなら so pleasant an evening の語順で、so a pleasant evening という並びは誤りです。(c)の that 節（結果）、(d)の不定詞、(e)の instead of＋動名詞はいずれも正しい形です。
m: such a ＋形＋名／so ＋形＋a ＋名

t: 誤り指摘：resemble は他動詞
p: (a)［Her younger brother］ (b)［resembles with］ (c)［their father not only］ (d)［in appearance but］ (e)［also in temperament.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (b) resembles with
(a) Her younger brother
(c) their father not only
(d) in appearance but
(e) also in temperament.
e: resemble は他動詞で「〜に似ている」の意味なので、前置詞 with は不要です。resembles their father が正しい形です。(c)〜(e)の not only … but also … は、in appearance と in temperament の前置詞句が対応していて、正しい形です。
m: resemble＋目的語（with なし）

t: 誤り指摘：approach は他動詞
p: (a)［As the train］ (b)［approached to the station,］ (c)［the passengers began］ (d)［to collect］ (e)［their luggage.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (b) approached to the station,
(a) As the train
(c) the passengers began
(d) to collect
(e) their luggage.
e: approach は他動詞で「〜に近づく」の意味なので、前置詞 to は不要です。approached the station が正しい形です。(a)の接続詞 as（〜するにつれて）、(c)(d)の begin to do は正しい形です。名詞の approach（接近）は to を伴うため、混同に注意します。
m: approach, reach, enter は前置詞なしで目的語をとる

t: 誤り指摘：条件節では未来を現在形で
p: (a)［We will cancel］ (b)［the outdoor concert］ (c)［if it will rain］ (d)［on Saturday,］ (e)［as the organisers have announced.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) if it will rain
(a) We will cancel
(b) the outdoor concert
(d) on Saturday,
(e) as the organisers have announced.
e: 時・条件を表す副詞節の中では、未来のことでも現在形を使います。if it will rain は誤りで、if it rains が正しい形です。主節の We will cancel は未来を表すのでそのままで正しいです。(e)の as 節は「〜が発表したとおり」の意味で、現在完了も正しいです。
m: 条件・時の副詞節では未来も現在形

t: 誤り指摘：wish の仮定法過去完了
p: He sometimes wishes (a)［that he studied］ (b)［harder when］ (c)［he was a student,］ (d)［but his habits］ (e)［have not changed.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (a) that he studied
(b) harder when
(c) he was a student,
(d) but his habits
(e) have not changed.
e: 過去の事実に反する願望は、wish の後で過去完了（仮定法過去完了）を使います。when he was a student（学生のとき）と過去を指しているので、that he had studied harder とすべきです。(c)の was は when 節の事実を述べる直説法の過去で正しく、(e)の現在完了も正しい形です。
m: 過去への願望：wish ＋ had p.p.

t: 誤り指摘：all の後の関係代名詞
p: (a)［Sam taught me］ (b)［all what］ (c)［he had learned］ (d)［during his years］ (e)［as a pilot.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (b) all what
(a) Sam taught me
(c) he had learned
(d) during his years
(e) as a pilot.
e: all, everything, anything などの不定代名詞を先行詞とする関係代名詞には that を使い、what は使えません。what はそれ自体が先行詞を含む（the thing which）ためです。all that he had learned が正しい形で、all what は誤りです。(c)の過去完了や(e)の as a pilot（〜として）は正しい形です。
m: all／everything の後は that（what は不可）

t: 誤り指摘：superior の比較対象
p: (a)［This new model］ (b)［is far superior］ (c)［than the older one］ (d)［in both speed］ (e)［and reliability.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) than the older one
(a) This new model
(b) is far superior
(d) in both speed
(e) and reliability.
e: superior, inferior, prefer などはラテン語系の比較表現で、than ではなく to を使います。したがって(c)は to the older one が正しい形で、than the older one が誤りです。far は比較を強める副詞で、(b)は正しい形です。(d)(e)の in both A and B も正しい形です。
m: superior／inferior to A（than は不可）

t: 誤り指摘：Only after の倒置
p: (a)［Only after］ (b)［the results were published］ (c)［the committee noticed］ (d)［that the data］ (e)［had been misread.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) the committee noticed
(a) Only after
(b) the results were published
(d) that the data
(e) had been misread.
e: Only＋副詞（句・節）が文頭に出ると、主節は疑問文の語順に倒置されます。the committee noticed は did the committee notice が正しい形です。(b)の従属節は倒置されず、(d)(e)の that 節の過去完了も、noticed より前の誤読を表すので正しい形です。
m: Only ＋副詞（句・節）が文頭なら主節を倒置

t: 誤り指摘：excited と exciting
p: (a)［The audience］ (b)［was so exciting］ (c)［by the final match］ (d)［that many people］ (e)［stood up and cheered.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (b) was so exciting
(a) The audience
(c) by the final match
(d) that many people
(e) stood up and cheered.
e: excite は「（人を）興奮させる」という他動詞なので、人が興奮している状態は過去分詞の excited で表し、exciting は「（物事が）人を興奮させるような」の意味になります。聴衆が試合に興奮したので was so excited が正しい形です。(c)の by は excited と結びつき、(d)(e)の so … that 構文の結果を表す節も正しい形です。
m: 人が感じる＝-ed、物事が感じさせる＝-ing

t: 誤り指摘：had better の否定
p: (a)［You had better］ (b)［not to］ (c)［leave valuables］ (d)［in the car］ (e)［overnight.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (b) not to
(a) You had better
(c) leave valuables
(d) in the car
(e) overnight.
e: had better の後には原形不定詞が続き、否定は had better not＋原形です。not to leave と to を付けるのは誤りで、not leave が正しい形です。(c)〜(e)の leave valuables in the car overnight は正しい語順です。
m: had better not ＋原形（to は不要）

t: 誤り指摘：It is kind of you to do
p: It was (a)［very kind］ (b)［for you］ (c)［to lend me］ (d)［your umbrella］ (e)［on such a rainy day.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (b) for you
(a) very kind
(c) to lend me
(d) your umbrella
(e) on such a rainy day.
e: kind, nice, polite, stupid など、人の性質を表す形容詞では、不定詞の意味上の主語は of＋人で表します。It was very kind of you to lend me … が正しい形で、for you は誤りです。(e)の such a rainy day は such a＋形容詞＋名詞で正しい形です。
m: 人の性質を表す形容詞は of ＋人

t: 誤り指摘：as … as の比較
p: Their new office (a)［is nearly］ (b)［twice as］ (c)［large than］ (d)［the old one,］ (e)［though the rent is similar.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) large than
(a) is nearly
(b) twice as
(d) the old one,
(e) though the rent is similar.
e: 倍数表現は twice as large as … で、as … as の形を保ちます。large than は誤りで、large as が正しい形です。than は比較級の後でしか使いません。(a)(b)の nearly twice as も正しい形で、(e)の though 節も問題ありません。
m: 倍数＋as 原級 as A

t: 誤り指摘：avoid は動名詞をとる
p: (a)［The mayor］ (b)［has avoided］ (c)［to answer］ (d)［questions about］ (e)［the new tax.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) to answer
(a) The mayor
(b) has avoided
(d) questions about
(e) the new tax.
e: avoid は動名詞だけを目的語にとる動詞で、to answer は誤りです。avoided answering が正しい形です。enjoy, finish, mind, consider, avoid, give up などは動名詞をとる動詞として覚えます。(b)の現在完了は正しい形です。
m: avoid／finish／mind＋動名詞

t: 誤り指摘：間接疑問の語順
p: Could you tell me (a)［where is］ (b)［the nearest post office］ (c)［and how long］ (d)［it takes］ (e)［to walk there?］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (a) where is
(b) the nearest post office
(c) and how long
(d) it takes
(e) to walk there?
e: tell の目的語になる疑問詞節（間接疑問）は、平叙文の語順（疑問詞＋S＋V）になります。where is the nearest post office は where the nearest post office is が正しい形です。(c)(d)の how long it takes は正しい語順で、(e)の to walk there も正しい形です。
m: 間接疑問は疑問詞＋S＋V

t: 誤り指摘：neither の倒置
p: (a)［I haven't read］ (b)［the report yet,］ (c)［and so］ (d)［has my colleague,］ (e)［as far as I know.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) and so
(a) I haven't read
(b) the report yet,
(d) has my colleague,
(e) as far as I know.
e: 否定文に続けて「〜もまた…ない」と言うときは neither（または nor）＋助動詞＋主語です。and so has my colleague は肯定の内容に使う言い方なので誤りで、and neither has my colleague が正しい形です。(e)の as far as I know は「私の知る限り」で正しい成句です。
m: 否定文を受けて「〜もない」＝neither＋助動詞＋S

t: 誤り指摘：現在完了と過去を表す語句
p: (a)［My cousin］ (b)［has lived］ (c)［in Osaka］ (d)［until last year,］ (e)［but now he lives in Kobe.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (b) has lived
(a) My cousin
(c) in Osaka
(d) until last year,
(e) but now he lives in Kobe.
e: until last year のように過去の一時点に終わったことを表す語句があるときは、現在完了ではなく過去形を使います。has lived は lived が正しい形です。現在完了は現在と結びつく経験・継続・完了を表します。(e)の now he lives は現在と対比していて正しいです。
m: 明確な過去の語句がある文は過去形

t: 誤り指摘：使役の受動態
p: (a)［The students］ (b)［were made］ (c)［clean］ (d)［the classroom］ (e)［after the festival.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) clean
(a) The students
(b) were made
(d) the classroom
(e) after the festival.
e: make が使役の意味で使われる能動態の make O do は、受動態では be made to do と to が復活します。were made clean は誤りで、were made to clean が正しい形です。能動態で They made the students clean the classroom. なら原形のままです。(e)の after the festival も正しいです。
m: make O do→be made to do（受動で to が復活）

t: 誤り指摘：until と by
p: Please make sure that you (a)［return］ (b)［the books to the library］ (c)［until Friday］ (d)［at the latest,］ (e)［or you will be charged a fine.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) until Friday
(a) return
(b) the books to the library
(d) at the latest,
(e) or you will be charged a fine.
e: until は「（ずっと）〜まで」と継続の期限を表し、by は「〜までに」と動作の期限を表します。「金曜日までに返却する」のは動作なので by Friday が正しく、until Friday は誤りです。at the latest（遅くとも）も by と相性のよい表現で、(e)の命令文の後の or（さもないと）も正しい形です。
m: until（まで継続）／by（までに完了）

t: 誤り指摘：devote oneself to＋動名詞
p: (a)［She devoted］ (b)［herself to］ (c)［improve］ (d)［the lives of］ (e)［homeless children.］
q: 次の英文の下線部（［ ］で示した(a)〜(e)）のうち、文法・語法上の誤りを含むものを1つ選びなさい。
c: (c) improve
(a) She devoted
(b) herself to
(d) the lives of
(e) homeless children.
e: devote oneself to ～は「〜に身をささげる」で、この to は前置詞なので後ろは名詞か動名詞です。improve は improving が正しい形です。同じ型には be committed to doing, look forward to doing などがあります。(a)の過去形と(d)(e)の名詞句は正しいです。
m: to＋動名詞：devote／be committed／object to

t: 整序：約束の内容
p: She promised me ( that / would / she / tell / what / no one / happened / had ).
q: 次の英文の（ ）内の語句を並べ替えて正しい英文を作るとき、5番目に来る語句を選びなさい。
c: no one
what
tell
would
e: 正しい文は She promised me that she would tell no one what had happened. です。that 節の中の語順は that(1) she(2) would(3) tell(4) no one(5) what(6) had(7) happened(8) で、5番目は no one です。what had happened は「何が起きたか」という名詞節で、tell の直接目的語になっています。
m: promise＋人＋that 節。tell no one＝だれにも話さない

t: 整序：There is no telling
p: With the weather changing so quickly in the mountains, ( no / is / telling / there / what / the afternoon / will / bring ).
q: 次の英文の（ ）内の語句を並べ替えて正しい英文を作るとき、4番目に来る語句を選びなさい。
c: telling
no
what
is
e: 正しい文は … there is no telling what the afternoon will bring. です。There is no doing は「〜することはできない」という慣用表現で、there(1) is(2) no(3) telling(4) what(5) the afternoon(6) will(7) bring(8) の語順になり、4番目は telling です。what 以下は「午後が何をもたらすか」という間接疑問で、平叙文の語順になります。
m: There is no doing＝〜することはできない

t: 整序：It never occurred to me
p: It ( never / me / occurred / that / to / the meeting / might / be cancelled ).
q: 次の英文の（ ）内の語句を並べ替えて正しい英文を作るとき、5番目に来る語句を選びなさい。
c: that
me
to
might
e: 正しい文は It never occurred to me that the meeting might be cancelled. です。it は that 節を指す形式主語で、never(1) occurred(2) to(3) me(4) that(5) the meeting(6) might(7) be cancelled(8) の語順になります。5番目は that です。occur to＋人は「人の心に浮かぶ」です。
m: It occurs to A that ～＝Aに～という考えが浮かぶ

t: 空所補充：非制限用法の which
p: The proposal was rejected, ( ) surprised no one in the office.
q: 次の英文の空所に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: which
what
that
it
e: 空所の前の文全体（提案が却下されたこと）を先行詞とする継続用法の関係代名詞は which です。コンマの後ろに続けるので that は使えません。what は先行詞を含む関係代名詞で、前に文があるこの場合には不適切です。it は接続詞がないままで二つの文をつなげる誤りになります。
m: 文全体を受ける関係詞は , which

t: 空所補充：未来完了
p: By the time the guests arrive tomorrow, we ( ) the preparations.
q: 次の英文の空所に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: will have finished
had finished
have finished
finished
e: By the time ～ は「〜までには」で、未来のある時点までに完了している動作を述べるので、未来完了 will have finished が適切です。had finished は過去のある時点までの完了（過去完了）、have finished は現在、finished は過去を表しており、どれも tomorrow と合いません。
m: By the time ～, ＋未来完了

t: 空所補充：関係代名詞 whose
p: This is the house ( ) roof was damaged in the storm last winter, and the owners are still waiting for the repairs to begin.
q: 次の英文の空所に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: whose
which
that
where
e: 空所の後に roof という名詞が続くので、所有を表す関係代名詞 whose が入ります（whose roof＝その家の屋根）。which と that は名詞の前に置けず、where は場所を表す関係副詞で、roof の前に置いて所有の意味にはなりません。
m: 関係詞＋名詞なら whose

t: 物語：夜の渡し船
p:
My father worked the night ferry for thirty years, and in all that time I never once saw him look at the water. He looked at the clock, the fuel gauge, the faces of the passengers as they came aboard, but never at the river itself, as if it were a colleague whose moods he knew too well to need to check. When I was twelve I asked him why. He said that a man who watches the water is a man who is hoping for it to be kind. 'You prepare for the worst and take the rest as a gift,' he said, and went back to counting the tickets.
I thought this a cold way to live. It was not until the winter he retired that I understood. We were crossing together on the last evening, and halfway over, the engine coughed and went silent. Before I had registered the silence, he was already moving: a torch in one hand, the spare line in the other, a calm instruction to the two passengers to sit. Within ten minutes we were drifting safely towards the landing. He never spoke of it afterwards. But that night, on the dark deck, I saw him look at the water for the first time, briefly, the way one nods to an old friend.
q: 本文の内容と一致するものを選びなさい。
c: The narrator's father avoided watching the water because he did not want to depend on its being kind to him.
The narrator's father never looked at the water because he had been frightened by an accident on the river long ago.
The narrator's father studied the passengers' faces in order to find those who had not bought tickets.
The narrator's father retired after the engine failure because the incident had made him lose his nerve completely.
e: 父は「水を見る人は、水が穏やかであることを期待している人だ」と話しています。つまり水に頼らず、最悪に備えるために見なかったのです。事故の恐怖、無賃乗車の探索、エンジン故障後の引退はいずれも本文にありません（引退は冬で、この夜が最後の運航の日です）。
m: 理由は発言の引用部分に書かれている

q: 語り手は父の生き方を I thought this a cold way to live と考えていましたが、のちに理解しました。その理由として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: The father's calm and quick action during the engine failure showed that his habit was a form of preparation, not coldness.
The father later confessed that he had been secretly afraid of the river for many years.
The narrator saw that the passengers admired the father more than any other member of the crew.
The narrator learned that the ferry had been unsafe throughout the thirty years of his father's service.

m: 後半の出来事が前半の考えをどう変えたかを追う

q: 本文の最後の the way one nods to an old friend が表す内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。

t: 評論：共有される休日
p: A holiday taken alone and a holiday taken with everyone else are quite different goods. This is the claim of those who defend fixed public holidays against the argument that workers would be happier if allowed to choose their own days off. The argument has some force: a person who rests when she is tired, and travels when the fares are low, gains something that a calendar cannot give. But rest, it turns out, has a social side. A free afternoon is worth more when friends and relatives are also free, and a town in which everything closes at once has a quality of stillness that cannot be had when half the shops stay open. In this respect shared time resembles a language: its value to each person depends on how many others use it. If we let every individual choose, we may well find that everyone has more freedom and yet that no one has the other people to spend it with.
q: この文章の主旨として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Rest is more valuable when shared, so fixed public holidays have a justification that individual choice cannot replace.
Workers who choose their own days off are less productive than those who follow a fixed calendar.
Public holidays should be abolished because many shops are unable to stay open on those days.
Travelling when the fares are low is a better use of free time than staying at home with friends.
e: 筆者は、休みには社会的な側面があり、友人や親族が同時に休めてこそ価値が高まるので、各人の自由な選択では置き換えられない、と述べています。生産性の比較、祝日廃止、旅行の優劣はいずれも本文の論点ではありません。個人選択の利点も認めた上での主張です。
m: 主旨は But 以降の部分に注目する

t: 評論：言語のような時間

q: 本文の shared time resembles a language の説明として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Its value to each person depends on how many other people take part in it.
It has to be learned in childhood, just as a person learns a first language.
It differs from one country to another according to the calendar that each follows.
It becomes richer and more valuable as it is used by a smaller number of people.
e: コロン以下に its value to each person depends on how many others use it とあります。言語は話す人が多いほど価値が高いのと同様に、共有される休みも同時に休む人が多いほど価値が高い、という類比です。幼少期の習得、国による違い、少数での使用はいずれも本文にありません（4番目は逆です）。
m: A resembles B の後のコロンが類似点の説明

t: 評論：自由と相手の不在
p: A holiday taken alone and a holiday taken with everyone else are quite different goods. This is the claim of those who defend fixed public holidays against the argument that workers would be happier if allowed to choose their own days off. q: 本文最後の文 everyone has more freedom and yet no one has the other people to spend it with が示す内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Individual freedom to choose days off can reduce the value of time off by removing its shared side.
People who are free to choose their days off will prefer to spend them alone at home.
The author expects all workers to choose the same days off if they are given the choice.
Freedom to choose days off is impossible to put into practice in any modern town or city.
e: 各人が休みを自由に選べば、自由は増えるが、一緒に過ごす相手がいなくなる、つまり休みの共有という価値が失われるというパラドクスです。2番目は選好の話、3番目は全員が同じ日を選ぶという予想で本文と逆、4番目は実施不可能とまでは言っていません。
m: and yet（それなのに）の前後の対比を読む

t: 評論：沈黙という合理的な選択
p: When a company announces that it welcomes new ideas, employees are often unconvinced, and their doubt is not unreasonable. An idea is a small risk taken by one person on behalf of the whole organization. If it succeeds, the credit is shared; if it fails, the blame tends to land on the one who proposed it. Under such conditions the sensible response is silence. Managers who complain that their staff lack imagination may therefore be mistaken about the cause. What is missing is not imagination but safety. Some firms have begun to hold meetings devoted to 'failures of the month', at which the leaders speak first about their own mistakes. The practice can seem theatrical, but its purpose is practical: it shows, more convincingly than any announcement, that an idea that does not work will not be held against the person who offered it.
q: 本文の Managers … may therefore be mistaken about the cause. について、筆者が考える社員の沈黙の本当の原因として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Employees stay silent because proposing an idea exposes them to blame if it fails.
Employees cannot think of new ideas unless they have received special training from the company.
Managers do not listen to the ideas that are offered to them in meetings.
Companies announce new ideas so often that their staff no longer believe any such announcement.
e: 成功すれば功績は共有されるが、失敗すれば提案者が責められるので、沈黙が合理的な反応になる、というのが筆者の説明です。したがって問題は想像力の欠如ではなく安全の欠如です。研修の不足、管理職が聞かないこと、発表の頻度は本文にありません。
m: What is missing is not A but B の B が原因

c: To show employees that an idea that fails will not be held against the person who offered it.
To embarrass the leaders into taking greater risks with the company's money.
To collect data on the number of ideas that fail in each month.

m: but 以降（its purpose is practical）に目的が書かれる

t: 物語：祖母の門
p: When Grandmother moved into the flat, the first thing she asked was where she could hang her gate. We laughed, because the gate was an old iron thing from the house she had left, rusted at the hinges, and the flat had no garden. She was not joking. She had brought it in the back of the van, wrapped in blankets like a patient, and for three weeks it leaned against the hall wall while she walked around it as if waiting for it to speak. Then, one Sunday, she asked my uncle to fix it to the balcony railing. It opened, if anyone dared to try it, onto a drop of four floors and a view of car roofs. But each evening she stood there with her tea, and once I heard her say 'Good evening' to the empty air, in the voice she used for neighbours. It took me a long time to understand that the gate had never been about the garden. It was something to open and close, a sign that a house had somebody coming and going.
q: We laughed の理由として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: The old gate seemed useless in a flat that had no garden.
The gate was far too heavy to be carried into the flat by one person.
Grandmother had never owned a gate before she moved into the flat.
Grandmother had said that she would sell the gate to a neighbour soon.
e: 直前に because 節があり、門は錆びた古い鉄製で、しかも新しい住まいには庭がなかったから笑った、とあります。重さ、初めて持つこと、売却の発言は本文に書かれておらず、「本気だった（She was not joking）」とも矛盾します。
m: We laughed, because … の because 節を確認する

c: She treated the gate with great care, as something precious to her.
The gate had been damaged in the move and needed repair by a skilled worker.
She was worried that the gate might be stolen from the van while it was parked.
She thought the gate was ill and wanted to cure it with care.
e: like a patient（患者のように）毛布にくるんで運んだ、という比喩は、祖母が門を大切に扱ったことを表します。実際に傷んだわけでも、盗難を心配したわけでも、門が病気だと考えたわけでもありません。比喩は字義どおりに取らず、態度を読み取ります。
m: like ～ の比喩は「どんな態度か」を読む

m: the gate had never been about the garden に注目

t: 評論：豆の数の推測
p: In classroom demonstrations, a jar of beans is passed around and each student writes down a guess at the number inside. The average of the guesses is usually closer to the truth than almost any individual guess. This is often taken as proof of the wisdom of crowds, but the demonstration works only under certain conditions. The guesses must be made independently, so that errors are scattered in all directions and cancel each other out. If the students see one another's answers, the errors start to point the same way, and the average is no better than that of the most confident person. Crowds, in other words, are wise only so long as their members are allowed to be separately mistaken. What the demonstration really shows is not that many heads are better than one, but that many independent heads are, and the difference is easily lost in the meetings where we most hope to use it.
q: 本文の内容と一致するものを選びなさい。
c: Averaging guesses works well only when the guesses are made independently of one another.
The average of the guesses is always more accurate than the best individual guess in the group.
Students who see one another's answers learn to give more accurate guesses.
The most confident person in a group usually gives the best estimate of the number in the jar.
e: 本文は、平均が正確になるのは推測が互いに独立している場合に限られる、と述べます。「常に最良の個人より正確」とは言っておらず、答えを見せ合うと誤りが同じ方向にそろって平均の精度が落ちます。最も自信のある人の推定が最良とも書かれていません。
m: only under certain conditions の条件を押さえる

t: 評論：誤差が同じ方向を向く
p: In classroom demonstrations, a jar of beans is passed around and each student writes down a guess at the number inside. q: 本文の the errors start to point the same way の意味として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Mistakes made by different people begin to be mistakes of the same kind.
People begin to correct one another's mistakes more and more quickly than before.
The errors become smaller as the guessers grow more and more confident.
All of the guesses begin to point towards the one correct number.
e: 独立した推測では誤りが四方に散って打ち消し合いますが、互いの答えを見ると、誤りが同じ向きにそろってしまい、打ち消し合わなくなります。2番目は訂正し合うこと、3番目は誤差の縮小、4番目は全員が正解に向かうことで、いずれも逆の意味です。
m: point the same way＝同じ方向の誤りにそろう

t: 評論：会議で失われるもの
p: In classroom demonstrations, a jar of beans is passed around and each student writes down a guess at the number inside. q: 本文最後の the difference is easily lost in the meetings where we most hope to use it の含意として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Group discussion often destroys the independence that makes the average of a crowd accurate.
Meetings are unnecessary because the average of many guesses is always correct.
People in meetings are too lazy to give opinions that differ from the average.
The beans in the jar cannot be counted accurately during a meeting.
e: the difference は「多数の頭」と「多数の独立した頭」の違いです。会議では他人の意見を聞きながら話すため、独立性が失われやすい、という含意です。会議が不要という話、怠惰という話、豆を数えられないという話は本文にありません。
m: the difference が何と何の違いかを確認する

t: 物語：天気予報屋の露店
p: The umbrella stall at the station exit was run by a man everyone called the Weatherman, though he had never been right about the weather. He sold more umbrellas on dry days than on wet ones, which puzzled the neighbourhood until a student asked him about it. 'On wet days,' he said, 'people are in a hurry and buy the first umbrella they see. They remember nothing about me. On dry days, they walk slowly and listen, and they buy because I have convinced them that the sky is lying.' He winked. 'And then it rains, and they come back to say I was right. I let them. It costs nothing, and it keeps the stall busy.' The student, who had expected a confession of fraud, found herself admiring him a little. He did not claim knowledge he lacked; he simply sold the possibility of rain, and people, who dislike being unprepared more than they dislike spending money, were happy to pay for it.
q: その男が乾いた日により多くの傘を売る理由として、本文から読み取れるものを選びなさい。
c: On dry days customers have time to listen, and he persuades them to prepare for rain.
He lowers his prices on dry days to attract customers who have no intention of using an umbrella.
His forecasts are more accurate on dry days than they are on wet days.
Dry days are the days when most people forget to bring their own umbrellas.
e: 男自身が、雨の日は急いでいて最初の傘を買うだけだが、晴れの日は人々がゆっくり歩いて話を聞き、空が嘘をついていると説得されて買う、と説明しています。値下げ、予報の精度、傘を忘れる日という説明は本文にありません。
m: 発言中の On dry days, … の部分が理由

t: 物語：詐欺の告白ではなかった
p: The umbrella stall at the station exit was run by a man everyone called the Weatherman, though he had never been right about the weather. He sold more umbrellas on dry days than on wet ones, which puzzled the neighbourhood until a student asked him about it. 'On wet days,' he said, 'people are in a hurry and buy the first umbrella they see. They remember nothing about me. On dry days, they walk slowly and listen, and they buy because I have convinced them that the sky is lying.' He winked. 'And then it rains, and they come back to say I was right. I let them. It costs nothing, and it keeps the stall busy.' The student, who had expected a confession of fraud, found herself admiring him a little. He did not claim knowledge he lacked; he simply sold the possibility of rain, and people, who dislike being unprepared more than they dislike spending money, were happy to pay for it.
q: 学生が男を少し称賛するようになった理由として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: He did not pretend to know the weather; he sold people protection against uncertainty.
He confessed that he earned his living by deceiving the students at the station.
He proved that his weather forecasts were right on almost every day of the whole year.
He gave umbrellas away for nothing to all of the people who were caught in the rain.
e: 学生は詐欺の告白を予期していましたが、男は知らないことを知っているふりをせず、雨の可能性を売っていました。したがって「不確かさへの備えを売る」というのが称賛の理由です。学生を欺く告白、予報の的中、傘の無料配布は本文にありません。
m: He did not claim knowledge he lacked に注目

t: 物語：人は何にお金を払うか

q: 本文最後の people … dislike being unprepared more than they dislike spending money の意味として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: People will spend money to avoid the discomfort of being caught without an umbrella.
People dislike spending money more than they dislike getting wet in the rain on their way home.
People who are unprepared for the rain usually refuse to buy anything at all from a stall.
People who spend a lot of money on umbrellas are always well prepared for every kind of weather.
e: dislike A more than B は「BよりもAを嫌う」で、準備不足のほうが出費よりも嫌いだ、ということです。したがって人は傘を持たずに困る不快さを避けるためにお金を払います。2番目は比較の向きが逆、3番目・4番目は本文にない一般化です。
m: dislike A more than B＝Bより A が嫌い

t: 評論：種子貯蔵庫と保険
p: Deep in a mountain, in a vault kept at temperatures well below freezing, lie millions of seeds from every part of the world. The collection is often called an insurance policy, and it is easy to see why: if a disease or a war destroys a crop variety in one country, a sample can be brought back from the vault. Yet the metaphor, though useful, hides a difficulty. An insurance policy pays out in money, which can buy whatever is needed. Seeds, by contrast, are living things that must be grown, renewed and tested every few decades, or they lose the ability to germinate. A stored variety is therefore not a thing that is safe once and for all; it needs people who go on caring about it. The vault protects the seeds, but only a continuing human effort protects the vault.
q: この文章の主旨として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: A seed bank cannot guarantee safety by itself, because stored seeds need continuing human care.
Seed banks are unnecessary because crop varieties are very rarely destroyed by disease or war in any country.
Insurance companies should pay for the maintenance of the seed vaults in every country of the world.
Seeds can be stored safely for several centuries without ever being grown or tested again in a laboratory.
e: 筆者は、種子貯蔵庫を保険にたとえる比喩の難点として、種子は生きており、数十年ごとに栽培・更新・検査をしなければ発芽力を失う、だから保管された品種を守るには人の継続的な努力が必要だ、と述べています。不要論、保険会社の負担、数世紀の保存はいずれも本文にありません。
m: Yet（しかし）以降に筆者の本題がある

t: 評論：比喩が隠す難点
p: Deep in a mountain, in a vault kept at temperatures well below freezing, lie millions of seeds from every part of the world. The collection is often called an insurance policy, and it is easy to see why: if a disease or a war destroys a crop variety in one country, a sample can be brought back from the vault. Yet the metaphor, though useful, hides a difficulty. An insurance policy pays out in money, which can buy whatever is needed. Seeds, by contrast, are living things that must be grown, renewed and tested every few decades, or they lose the ability to germinate. A stored variety is therefore not a thing that is safe once and for all; it needs people who go on caring about it. The vault protects the seeds, but only a continuing human effort protects the vault.
q: 本文の the metaphor … hides a difficulty の difficulty として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Unlike money, seeds are living things that lose their value unless they are renewed.
Insurance policies cannot be used when a war has destroyed a crop variety in one country.
Seeds are far more expensive to store than most other kinds of valuable goods in the world.
The temperature of the vault is too low for the seeds to survive for a long time.
e: 直後に、保険金は何でも買えるお金で払われるが、種子は生きていて更新しなければ発芽力を失う、とあります。これが比喩の隠す難点です。保険の適用不能、費用の高さ、温度の低さは本文にありません（氷点下の低温は、本文では種子を保管する条件として述べられています）。
m: A, by contrast, B の対比が難点を示す

t: 評論：街角の店の価値
p: Economists measure the value of a shop by what it sells, but this misses much of what a small shop gives to its street. The owner of a corner shop usually knows which customers live alone, which elderly neighbours have not been seen for a few days, and which children are walking home from school unaccompanied. None of this knowledge appears in the accounts, yet it is of real use to the neighbourhood. When such a shop closes, the loss to the street is not only the convenience of buying milk close to home; it is also the quiet network of attention that the shop provided without any cost to the public purse. Supermarkets, with their lower prices and wider choice, may well be better at selling goods. The point is that selling goods was never the only thing the corner shop was doing, and a way of counting that sees only sales will always conclude that the shop is unnecessary.
q: この文章の主旨として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: The value of a small shop includes social benefits that do not appear in its sales figures.
Supermarkets bring no benefit to a neighbourhood apart from their lower prices and wider choice of goods.
Corner shop owners should be paid by the government for watching over the people in their neighbourhoods.
Elderly people ought to avoid shopping at supermarkets in order to protect the small shops near their homes.
e: 筆者は、小さな店は商品を売るだけでなく、一人暮らしの人や高齢者、子どもたちへの見守りという、会計に表れない価値を街に与えていると述べます。スーパーの利点も認めているので、2番目の「何の利益もない」は誤りで、政府の支払いや高齢者への忠告も述べていません。
m: May well … The point is that … で譲歩→本題を読む

t: 評論：売上だけを数える見方

q: 本文最後の a way of counting that sees only sales will always conclude that the shop is unnecessary の意味として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: If only sales are counted, the other contributions of the shop are overlooked and it seems useless.
If sales are counted carefully, it can be shown that corner shops earn more money than supermarkets.
Because corner shops sell so few goods, even accurate accounts show that they are unnecessary to the street.
Because the shop provides attention without charge, its accounts always show a loss.
e: 売上だけを数える方法では、見守りなど売上に表れない貢献が見落とされ、店は不要に見える、という意味です。2番目の「売上で勝つ」、3番目の「正確な会計でも不要」、4番目の「常に赤字」は、本文の主張とは異なります。筆者は計算方法の限界を批判しています。
m: a way of counting＝評価の物差しの限界を指摘

t: 物語：舟小屋の兄弟
p: After the funeral, my brother and I found ourselves at the old boat shed, because neither of us knew where else to go. Our father's skiff was still on its trestles, half-planked, as he had left it in the autumn. 'Somebody ought to finish it,' Daiki said, and then, as if he had said something dangerous, looked at the floor. We had not spoken of what we would do with the house or the boat or the fishing licence, and I had been grateful for the silence. I picked up a plane from the bench. It fitted my hand in a way that surprised me; the handle was worn smooth in exactly the place where my fingers wanted to rest. We worked for three hours that afternoon without saying more than 'hold this' and 'higher'. When we stopped, the light had gone and the boat looked no more finished than before. But I noticed that Daiki's shoulders, which he had held like a coat-hanger for a week, had come down, and I suspected that mine had as well.
q: 二人が舟小屋にいた理由として本文から読み取れるものを選びなさい。
c: They did not know where else to go after the funeral.
They had promised their father that they would finish the skiff.
They wanted to sell the skiff before the family left the town.
Their father had asked them in his will to repair the boat shed.
e: 冒頭に because neither of us knew where else to go（二人とも他に行く場所が分からなかったから）とあります。父との約束、売却の意図、遺言は本文に書かれておらず、むしろ家・船・漁業権について話し合ってもいませんでした。
m: 冒頭の because 節に理由がある

t: 物語：床を見た Daiki

c: He felt that speaking about finishing the boat might be too painful or too bold so soon after the funeral.

He realised that the skiff was too badly damaged to be repaired by the two of them.

m: as if ～ が示す気持ちを読み取る

q: 本文最後の Daiki's shoulders … had come down が示す内容として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: Working together on the boat eased the tension that the brothers had been feeling.

e: 肩が下りたのは緊張がほぐれたことを表します。直前に、舟は前より完成していないとあるので、完成の安堵ではなく、黙って一緒に作業したことが緊張を和らげたと読めます。家や漁業権の決定、舟の売却合意は本文にありません。
m: 身体の描写は気持ちの変化を示す

t: 物語：赤ペンの先生
p: Mrs Okada had a reputation for the red pen. Essays came back from her covered in marks, and the pupils joked that she bled on their pages. I was fifteen, and I hated her for it, partly because the marks were always right. One afternoon she kept me behind after class. I expected a lecture. Instead she handed me an essay from the previous term, with her usual corrections, and asked me to read only the comments in the margin. 'What do you notice?' she said. I looked. Most of them were questions: Why this word? What do you mean here? Is this what you really think? 'I never correct what I don't expect to improve,' she said. 'If I stopped marking your work, that would be the day I had given up on you.' She said nothing more, and I left feeling oddly embarrassed, as if I had been caught complaining about a gift. The next week I started writing my essays as if she were reading over my shoulder. It was exhausting. It was also the first time anyone had made me feel that what I wrote was worth arguing with.
q: Mrs Okada が語り手を放課後に残した目的として最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: She wanted the narrator to see that her comments were questions meant to provoke thought.
She wanted to scold the narrator for criticising her marking in front of the other pupils.
She wished to praise the narrator for the great progress made over the previous term.
She intended to tell the narrator that future essays would be marked less strictly.
e: 語り手は説教を予期しましたが、先生は前学期の答案を渡し、余白のコメントだけを読ませました。コメントの多くは問いかけで、先生は「直らないと思う人の答案は直さない」と話します。目的は、コメントが考えさせる問いだと気づかせることです。叱責、称賛、採点を緩めるという話は本文にありません。
m: Instead 以降の行動に目的が表れる

t: 物語：贈り物への不満

q: 本文の as if I had been caught complaining about a gift が表す気持ちとして最も適切なものを選びなさい。
c: The narrator realised that her strict marking had been a kind of care all along.
The narrator felt rewarded for a piece of work that did not really deserve any reward.
The narrator felt that the teacher had given a present as an apology for her strict marking.
The narrator was ashamed that the essay had been the worst in the whole class that term.
e: 赤ペンの添削を恨んでいたが、それが「期待している生徒にだけ行う手間」だと分かり、贈り物に文句を言っているところを見つかったような気恥ずかしさを感じた、という流れです。報酬、謝罪の贈り物、クラスで最低という話は本文にありません。
m: gift＝先生の厳しい添削という好意

t: 物語：議論するに値する文章
p: Mrs Okada had a reputation for the red pen. Essays came back from her covered in marks, and the pupils joked that she bled on their pages. I was fifteen, and I hated her for it, partly because the marks were always right. One afternoon she kept me behind after class. I expected a lecture. Most of them were questions: Why this word? What do you mean here? Is this what you really think? 'I never correct what I don't expect to improve,' she said. 'If I stopped marking your work, that would be the day I had given up on you.' She said nothing more, and I left feeling oddly embarrassed, as if I had been caught complaining about a gift.
